			<font style="display: inline;">unanticipated costs which may be incurred from time to time in connection with litigation, regulation and compliance, loan analyses and modifications or other contingencies.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

			<a name="Business"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">ITEM 1. BUSINESS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:center;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We are a diversified financial services holding company focused on delivering a broad range of investment banking, commercial banking and related financial services to corporate, individual and institutional investors, broker/dealers, governmental entities and financial intermediaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are the largest full-service brokerage firm headquartered in the Southwestern United States (based on the number of financial advisors).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">For purposes of this report, unless the context otherwise indicates, references to &#x201C;we,&#x201D; &#x201C;us,&#x201D; &#x201C;our,&#x201D; &#x201C;SWS&#x201D; and the &#x201C;company&#x201D; mean SWS Group, Inc. collectively with all of our subsidiaries, and references to "SWS Group" mean solely SWS Group, Inc. as a single entity.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS Group is a Delaware corporation that was incorporated in 1972, and that has its common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange (&#x201C;NYSE&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Our principal executive offices are located at 1201 Elm Street, Suite 3500, Dallas, Texas 75270.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our telephone number is (214) 859-1800 and our website is www.swsgroupinc.com.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not intend for information contained on our website to be part of this Form 10-K.&nbsp;&nbsp;We file annual, quarterly and current reports, proxy statements and other information with the SEC.&nbsp;&nbsp;You may read and copy any document we file with the SEC at the SEC&#x2019;s public reference room at 100 F Street, N.E., Washington, DC 20549.&nbsp;&nbsp;Please call the SEC at 1-800-SEC-0330 for information on the public reference room. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The SEC also maintains an Internet site at www.sec.gov that contains our annual, quarterly and current reports, proxy and information statements and other electronic filings.&nbsp;&nbsp;We make available free of charge on or through our website our annual, quarterly and current reports and amendments to those reports as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file such material with or furnish it to the SEC.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we will provide electronic or paper copies of our filings free of charge upon request. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our principal brokerage subsidiary, Southwest Securities, Inc. (&#x201C;Southwest Securities&#x201D;), is a registered broker/dealer and a member of the NYSE.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is also a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (&#x201C;FINRA&#x201D;), Securities Investor Protection Corporation (&#x201C;SIPC&#x201D;), and other regulatory and trade organizations.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Southwest Securities provides integrated trade execution, clearing and client account processing to over 150 financial service organizations, which includes correspondent broker/dealers and registered investment advisors in 29 states and Canada.&nbsp;&nbsp;Southwest Securities serves individual investors through its private client group offices in Texas, California and Oklahoma and also serves institutional investors nationwide.&nbsp;&nbsp;Southwest Securities also extends margin credit and lends securities and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">manages and participates in underwriting equity and fixed income securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2013, revenues from Southwest Securities accounted for approximately 73% of our consolidated revenues.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We also operate SWS Financial Services, Inc. (&#x201C;SWS Financial&#x201D;), a broker/dealer subsidiary that is also registered with FINRA.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS Financial contracts with 297 individual registered representatives (who are FINRA licensed salespersons) for the administration of their securities business.&nbsp;&nbsp;While these registered representatives must conduct all of their securities business through SWS Financial, they may separately conduct insurance, real estate brokerage or other business for other companies or for their own accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The registered representatives are responsible for all of their direct expenses and are paid higher commission rates than Southwest Securities' registered representatives to compensate them for their added expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS Financial is a correspondent of Southwest Securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We offer full-service, traditional and Internet banking through Southwest Securities, FSB (the &#x201C;Bank&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank is a federally chartered savings bank, organized and existing under the laws of the United States and regulated since July 21, 2011 by the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (the &#x201C;OCC&#x201D;).</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Prior to July 21, 2011, the Bank was regulated by the Office of Thrift Supervision (&#x201C;OTS&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;As of July 21, 2011, the Federal Reserve Board (&#x201C;FRB&#x201D;) began supervising and regulating SWS Group and SWS Banc Holdings, Inc. (&#x201C;SWS Banc&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank conducts business from its main operating facilities and headquarters in Dallas, Texas and 9 banking center locations in Texas and New Mexico. In 2003, SWS Banc was incorporated in the state of Delaware as a wholly-owned subsidiary of SWS Group, and became the sole stock</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">holder of the Bank in 2004.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:0pt;text-align:left;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">PRODUCTS AND SERVICES</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In fiscal 2013, we operated through four business segments grouped primarily by products, services and customer base: clearing, retail, institutional and banking.&nbsp;&nbsp;The segments are managed separately based on the types of products and services offered and their related client bases and are consistent with how we manage our resources and assess our performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;For more information about each of these business segments, see Item 7.&nbsp;&nbsp;&#x201C;Management&#x2019;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations,&#x201D; below.&nbsp;&nbsp;See also </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 23</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2013, June 29, 2012 and June 24, 2011 included under Item 8. &#x201C;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#x201D; for information regarding the revenues, income (loss) and total assets of each of our business segments</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Clearing.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Our Clearing segment provides clearing and execution services for other broker/dealers (predominantly on a fully disclosed basis).&nbsp;&nbsp;Our clientele includes general securities broker/dealers and firms specializing in high-volume trading.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In a fully disclosed clearing transaction, the identity of the clearing client&#x2019;s (&#x201C;correspondent&#x201D;) customer is known to us and we physically maintain the client&#x2019;s account and perform a variety of services as agent for the correspondent.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues in this segment are generated primarily through transaction charges to our correspondent firms for clearing their trades accord</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">ing to a contractual schedule.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In addition to clearing trades, we tailor our services to meet the specific needs of our clients and offer products and services such as recordkeeping, trade reporting, accounting, general back-office support, securities and margin lending, reorganization assistance and custody of securities.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We currently support a wide range of clearing clients, including discount and full-service brokerage firms, direct access firms, registered investment advisors and institutional firms.&nbsp;&nbsp;High-volume trading firms trade actively on a proprietary basis or provide services to those customers who trade actively on a daily basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of June 30, 2013, we provided clearing services for two high-volume trading firms.&nbsp;&nbsp;The nature of services provided to the customers of high-volume trading firms and the internal costs necessary to support them are substantially lower than the standard correspondent costs and services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, fees for services to these correspondents, on a per trade basis, are discounted substantially from the fees normally charged to other customers.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The terms of our agreements with our correspondents define the allocation of financial, operational and regulatory responsibility arising from the clearing relationship.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that the correspondent has available financial resources, we are protected against claims by customers of the correspondent arising from actions by the correspondent; however, if the correspondent is unable to meet its financial obligations, dissatisfied customers may attempt to recover from us.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Retail. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Retail segment includes the sale of retail securities, insurance products and managed accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;This segment generates revenue primarily through commissions charged on securities transactions, fees from managed accounts and the sale of insurance products as well as net interest income from retail customer account balances.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Retail Securities</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> We act as securities broker for retail investors in the purchase and sale of securities, options, commodities and futures contracts that are traded on various exchanges or in the over-the-counter market through our employee registered representatives or our independent contractor arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a securities broker, we extend margin credit on a secured basis to our retail customers in order to facilitate securities transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Through our insurance subsidiaries, we hold insurance licenses in 44 states in order to facilitate the sale of insurance and annuity products by our financial advisors to retail clients.&nbsp;&nbsp;In most cases, we charge commissions to our clients in accordance with our established commission schedule, subject to certain discounts based upon the client&#x2019;s level of business, the trade size and other relevant factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of our registered representatives also maintain licenses to sell certain insurance products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Southwest Securities is registered with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission ("CFTC") as a non-guaranteed introducing broker and is a member of the National Futures Association ("NFA").&nbsp;&nbsp;Southwest Securities is also a fully disclosed client of two of the largest futures commission merchants in the United States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our financial advisors work with their individual clients to create investment portfolios based on the client's specific financial goals and tolerance for risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;We provide access to fee-based platforms and a wide array of products and services including access to investment management programs that can be tailored to the individual client relationship to enhance the financial advisor's business and benefit his or her clients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">At June 30, 2013, Southwest Securities employed 167 registered representatives in 17 retail brokerage offices (one located in each of Austin, Dallas, Georgetown, Houston, League City, Longview, Lufkin, Plano, San Antonio and Southlake, Texas; one located in each of Oklahoma City and Norman, Oklahoma; one located in each of Beverly Hills, Monterey, Sacramento, San Diego and San Francisco, California).&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, at June 30, 2013, SWS Financial had contracts with 297 independent retail representatives for the administration of their securities business.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Insurance.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Southwest Financial Insurance Agency, Inc. and Southwest Insurance Agency, Inc (collectively, "SWS Insurance") hold insurance agency licenses in 44 states to allow our registered representatives to sell insurance and annuity products to their retail customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We retain no underwriting risk related to the insurance and annuity products that SWS Insurance sells.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Managed Accounts.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Through the Investment Management Group of Southwest Securities, we provide a number of advisory programs that offer advisors a wide array of products and services for their advisory business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 8pt">

			<a href="#IndexToAnnualReport"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:8pt;">Table Of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Margin Lending</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;We extend credit on a secured basis directly to our customers, the customers of correspondent firms and the correspondent firms themselves in order to facilitate securities transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;This credit, which generates interest income, is known as "margin lending" and is conducted primarily in our clearing and retail segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;We extend margin credit to correspondent firms only to the extent that such firms pledge their own ("proprietary") assets as collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our correspondents are required to indemnify us against margin losses in their customers&#x2019; accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because we must rely on the guarantees and general creditworthiness of our correspondents, we may be exposed to significant risk of loss if they are unable to meet their financial commitments should there be a substantial adverse change in the value of the margined securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In customer margin transactions, the client borrows money from us to purchase securities or for other purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loan is collateralized by the securities purchased or by other securities owned by the client.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest is charged to clients on the amount borrowed to finance margin transactions at a floating rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The rate charged is dependent on the average net debit balance in the client&#x2019;s accounts, the activity level in the accounts and the applicable cost of funds.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of the loan is subject to the margin regulations ("Regulation T") of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, FINRA margin requirements and our internal policies.&nbsp;&nbsp;In most transactions, Regulation T limits the amount loaned to a customer for the purchase of securities to 50% of the purchase price.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, in the event of a decline in the value of the collateral, FINRA requirements regulate the percentage of client cash or securities that must be on deposit as collateral for the loan. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In permitting clients to purchase on margin, we are subject to the risk that the value of our collateral could fall below the amount of that client's indebtedness.&nbsp;&nbsp;Agreements with margin account clients permit us to liquidate the clients&#x2019; securities with or without prior notice in the event of an insufficient amount of margin collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Despite those agreements, we may be unable to liquidate the clients&#x2019; securities for various reasons including, but not limited to, a thin trading market, an excessive concentration or the issuance of a trading halt.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The primary source of funds to finance client margin account balances is credit balances in the client&#x2019;s account.&nbsp;&nbsp;We generally pay interest to clients on these credit balances at a rate determined periodically.&nbsp;&nbsp;SEC regulations restrict the use of client funds to the financing of client activities including margin account balances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Excess customer credit balances, as defined by SEC regulations, are invested in short-term securities segregated for the exclusive benefit of customers as required by SEC regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;We generate net interest income when there is a positive interest rate spread between the rate earned from margin lending and segregated short-term investments and the rate paid on customer credit balances.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">I</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">nstitutional.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Institutional segment is comprised of businesses serving institutional customers in the areas of securities borrowing and lending, municipal finance, investment banking, fixed income sales and equity trading. Revenues in the institutional segment are derived from the net interest spread on stock loan transactions, commission and trading income from fixed income and equity products and investment banking fees from taxable and municipal securities transactions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Securities Lending Activiti</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">es.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Our securities borrowing and lending business includes borrowing and lending securities for other broker/dealers, lending institutions and our own clearing and retail operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;These activities involve borrowing securities to cover short sales and to complete transactions in which clients have failed to deliver securities by the required settlement date and lending securities to other broker/dealers for similar purposes.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">When borrowing securities, we are required to deposit cash or other collateral or to post a letter of credit with the lender, and we generally receive a rebate (based on the amount of cash deposited) or a fee calculated to yield a negotiated rate of return.&nbsp;&nbsp;When lending securities, we receive cash or similar collateral and generally pay interest (based on the amount of cash deposited) to the other party to the transaction.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, we earn net interest income based on the spread between the interest rate on cash or similar collateral we deposit and the interest rate paid on cash or similar collateral we receive. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Securities borrowing and lending transactions are executed pursuant to written agreements with counterparties that generally require securities borrowed and loaned to be marked-to-market on a daily basis, excess collateral to be refunded, and deficit collateral to be furnished.&nbsp;&nbsp;Collateral adjustments are made on a daily basis through the facilities of various clearinghouses.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are a principal in these securities borrowing and lending transactions and are liable for losses in the event of a failure of any other party to honor its contractual obligation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our management sets credit limits with each counterparty and reviews these limits regularly to monitor the risk level with each counterparty.&nbsp;&nbsp;The securities lending business is conducted primarily from Southwest Securities&#x2019; New Jersey office using a specialized sales force.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Municipal Finance.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Our municipal finance business</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> earns investment banking revenues by assisting public entity clients in meeting their financial needs and advising them on the most advantageous means of raising capital.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our municipal finance professionals assist public bodies in originating, syndicating and distributing securities of municipalities and political subdivisions. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Southwest Securities maintains municipal finance branch offices in Allen, Austin, Dallas and San Antonio, Texas; Aliso Viejo, Cardiff,&nbsp;&nbsp;Encino and Huntington Beach, California; Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, Chicago, Illinois, New York, New York, Albuquerque, New Mexico; Charlotte, North Carolina; Lexington, Kentucky; Columbia, South Carolina and Memphis Tennessee.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Participation in firm commitment municipal underwritings can expose us to material risk because we may not be able to sell the securities we have committed to purchase at the initial offering price.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, federal and state securities laws and regulations also affect the activities of underwriters and impose substantial potential liabilities for violations of such laws and regulations in connection with sales of securities by underwriters to the public.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Fixed Income Sales and Equity Trading.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Our fixed income sales and trading group specializes in trading and underwriting U.S. government and agency bonds, corporate bonds, municipal bonds, mortgage-backed, asset-backed and commercial mortgage-backed securities and structured products.&nbsp;&nbsp;The clients of our fixed income group include corporations, insurance companies, banks, mutual funds, money managers and other institutions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Southwest </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Securities has fixed income offices in Dallas and The Woodlands, Texas; Encino and San Francisco, California; Aspen and Evergreen, Colorado; Ft. Lauderdale and Palm Beach Gardens, Florida; Chicago, Illinois; Bloomfield, New Jersey; New York, New York and Memphis, Tennessee.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our equity trading department focuses on providing best execution for equity and option orders for&nbsp;clients.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also execute institutional portfolio trades and are a market maker in a limited number of listed securities.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our syndicate department, housed within our fixed income sales group, coordinates the distribution of managed and co-managed corporate equity underwritings, accepts invitations to participate in competitive or negotiated underwritings managed by other investment banking firms and allocates and markets our selling allotments to institutional clients and to other broker/dealers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:0pt;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Banking.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;The Banking segment offers traditional banking products and services through 9 full-service banking centers with nine banking centers located in Texas, one located in each of Arlington, Dallas, El Paso, Fort Worth, Granbury, Southlake and Waxahachie, and one located in each of Albuquerque and Ruidoso, New Mexico .&nbsp;&nbsp;Our focus in business banking includes small business ("SBA") lending.&nbsp;&nbsp;We originate the majority of our loans internally, and we believe this business model helps us build more valuable rel</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">ationships with our customers. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank offers a full array of deposit products, including checking, savings, money market and certificates of deposit.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a full-service lender, the Bank offers competitive rates and terms on business loans, as well as a full line of consumer loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;Customers have access to comprehensive Internet banking services and online bill payment.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank offers commercial loans, commercial real estate loans and consumer loans, primar</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">ily in Texas and New Mexico.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our mortgage purchase division purchases participations and sub-participations in newly originated residential loans (mainly 1-4 family residential loans) from various mortgage bankers nationwide.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2012, the Bank signed a sub-participation agreement with a non-affiliate bank to sub-participate in this bank&#x2019;s mortgage purchase program.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have made a maximum total commitment of $20.0 million pursuant to this agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loans are pre-committed for sale by the mortgage company to secondary investors.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of June 30, 2013, none of the $174.0 million purchased mortgage loans held for investment balance was from this sub-participation agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchased mortgage loans held for investment are held by the Bank on average for 25 days or less.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 95% of the loans conform to the standards of Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae, and the rest are &#x201C;A&#x201D; credit jumbo loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of the date of this report, the Bank had approximately 50 customer/originators across the nation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the Bank is exposed to credit risk before the loans are sold by the mortgage company, currently there is no recourse to the Bank after the mortgage company sells the lo</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">an to the secondary investor.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank earns substantially all of its revenues on the spread between the rates charged to customers on loans and the rates paid to depositors.</font>
		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt 36pt;text-indent: -36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Univers (W1);font-weight:bold;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">C</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">OMPETITION</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We encounter intense competition in our businesses.&nbsp;&nbsp;We compete directly with securities firms and banks, many of which have substantially greater capital and other resources than we have.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also encounter competition from insurance companies and financial institutions in many elements of our businesses. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The brokerage entities compete with other brokerage and financial services companies principally on the basis of service, product selection, price, location and reputation.&nbsp;&nbsp;We operate at a price disadvantage to discount brokerage firms that do not offer equivalent services.&nbsp;&nbsp;We compete for the correspondent clearing business on the basis of service, reputation, financial strength, price, technology and product selection.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Competition for successful securities traders, stock loan professionals and investment bankers among securities firms and other competitors is intense, as is competition for experienced financial advisors.&nbsp;&nbsp;We recognize the importance of hiring and retaining skilled professionals so we invest heavily in the recruiting process.&nbsp;&nbsp;The failure to attract and retain skilled professionals could have a material adverse effect on our business and on our performance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank also operates in an intensely competitive environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;This environment includes other banks, credit unions, nonbank lenders and insurance companies.&nbsp;&nbsp;The competition ranges from small community banks to large multinational commercial banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;As with the securities industry, the ability to attract and retain skilled professionals is critical to the Bank&#x2019;s success.&nbsp;&nbsp;To enhance these activities the Bank utilizes SWS for assistance in recruiting and educational programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank competes for community banking customers locally based on reputation, service, location and price.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank also competes nationally for the purchase of residential loans through its mortgage purchased division.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt 36pt;text-indent: -36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Univers (W1);font-weight:bold;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">REGULATION </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We operate in the financial services industry as, among other things, a securities broker/dealer, an SEC registered investment adviser and a bank. As a result, our businesses are highly regulated by U.S. federal and state regulatory agencies, self-regulatory organizations and national securities exchanges and, to a lesser extent, by foreign governmental agencies and financial regulatory bodies.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a matter of public policy, regulatory bodies in the United States are charged with, among other things, safeguarding the integrity of the securities and other financial markets and with protecting the interests of customers, including depositors, the Federal Deposit Insurance Fund (&#x201C;DIF&#x201D;), and the banking system as a whole, not with protecting the interests of regulated </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">entities or their creditors or stockholders. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Significant</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> laws and regulations that are applicable to us are described below. The description is a summary that is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the statutes, regulations and policies that are described. Also, such statutes, regulations and policies are continually under review by Congress and state legislatures and federal, state and other regulatory bodies. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> are regulated by the SEC and are subject to the disclosure and regulatory requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act") and the regulations promulgated hereunder, as administered by the SEC.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">As a public company with common stock listed on the NYSE, we are subject to corporate governance requirements established by the SEC and the NYSE, as well as federal and state law. Under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, as amended (the &#x201C;Sarbanes- Oxley Act&#x201D;), we are required to meet certain requirements regarding business dealings with members of our Board of Directors, the structure of our Audit Committee and ethical standards for our senior financial officers. Also, under Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, we are required to assess the effectiveness of our internal controls over financial reporting and to obtain an opinion from our independent auditors regarding the effectiveness of our internal controls over financial reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under SEC and NYSE rules, we are required to comply with other standards of corporate governance, including having a majority of independent directors serve on our Board of Directors, and the establishment of independent audit, compensation and corporate governance committees.&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS Group is a legal entity that is separate and distinct from its banking and non-banking subsidiaries. The principal sources of funds for SWS Group are cash dividends paid by its subsidiaries, capital contributions from the sale of its securities, investment income, and borrowings. Federal laws normally limit the amount of dividends or other capital distributions that a banking institution can pay, and the Bank must obtain prior approval from the OCC before it can pay dividends to us.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Due to the economic crisis, many new regulations and statutes have been proposed or enacted over the past several years</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> th</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">at contain wide-ranging proposals for altering the structures, regulations and competitive relationships of financial institutions operating and doing business in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most notably, on July 21, 2010, the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the &#x201C;Dodd-Frank Act&#x201D;) was enacted. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Dodd-Frank Act sought to restore responsibility and accountability to the U.S. financial system by significantly altering the regulation of financial institutions and the financial services industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most of the provisions contained in the Dodd-</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:1.8pt">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">From time to time, various legislative and regulatory initiatives are introduced in Congress and state legislatures, as well as by regulatory bodies.&nbsp;&nbsp;These initiatives may include proposals to expand or contract the powers of holding companies and depository institutions or proposals to substantially change the regulatory system for financial institutions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such legislation could change banking and brokerage statutes and our operating environment in substantial and unpredictable ways.&nbsp;&nbsp;If enacted, such legislation or regulatory changes could increase or decrease our cost of doing business (including increased compliance costs), limit or expand permissible activities or affect the competitive balance among banks, savings associations, credit unions, and other financial institutions.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot predict whether any such legislation or regulatory initiatives will be enacted, and, if enacted, the impact that it, and any implementing regulations, would have on our financial condition or results of operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any change in statutes, regulations or regulatory policies, or their implementation, interpretation, or enforcement, applicable to us or any of our subsidiaries could have a material adverse effect on our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:10.5pt;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Regulation of SWS Group</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS Group is regulated under the Savings and Loan Holding Company Act, as amended (the &#x201C;SLHC Act&#x201D;), and its subsidiaries that are not functionally regulated are subject to inspection, examination and supervision by the FRB. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 10pt">

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The FRB has the power to order any savings and loan holding company or its subsidiaries to terminate any activity or to terminate its ownership or control of any subsidiary when the FRB has reasonable grounds to believe that continuation of such activity or such ownership or control constitutes a serious risk to the financial soundness, safety or stability of any bank subsidiary of the holding company.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Dodd-Frank Act requires the federal financial regulatory agencies to adopt rules that prohibit banks and their affiliates from engaging in proprietary trading and investing in and sponsoring certain unregistered investment companies (including hedge funds and private equity funds), subject to certain exceptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;This provision is commonly called the &#x201C;Volcker Rule&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In October 2011 and January 2012, federal regulators proposed rules to implement the Volcker Rule. The proposed rules are highly complex, and many aspects of their application remain uncertain.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">FRB policy has historically required bank holding companies to act as a source of financial and managerial strength to their subsidiary banks. The Dodd-Frank Act codified this policy as a statutory requirement for savings and loan holding companies, including SWS Group. Under this requirement, SWS Group is expected to commit resources to support the Bank, including at times when it may not be in a financial position to provide such resources. Any capital loans by a holding company to any of its subsidiary banks are subordinate in right of payment to depositors and to certain other indebtedness of such subsidiary banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event of a holding company&#x2019;s bankruptcy, any commitment by the holding company to a federal bank regulatory agency to maintain the capital of a subsidiary bank will be assumed by the bankruptcy trustee and entitled to priority of payment. The implementing regulations for the &#x201C;source of strength&#x201D; statute have not been proposed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Regulation of the Securities Business.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> The securities industry in the United States is subject to extensive regulation under federal and state laws and regulations. Our U.S. broker/dealer subsidiaries are registered as such with the SEC and FINRA.&nbsp;&nbsp;Self-regulatory organizations such as FINRA have also enacted rules (which are subject to approval by the SEC) that govern their members and the industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;Securities firms are subject to regulation by state securities commissions in the states in which they conduct business. Southwest Securities and SWS Financial are registered in all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Southwest Securities is also registered in the U.S. Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico.&nbsp;&nbsp;Federal, state and other regulatory authorities have the power to undertake periodic examinations of our securities broker/dealer operations for the purpose of assuring our compliance with the applicable rules and regulations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Broker/dealers are subject to regulations that cover all aspects of the securities business, including the manner in which securities transactions are effected, net capital requirements, recordkeeping and reporting procedures, relationships and conflicts with customers, the handling of cash and margin accounts, sales methods and conduct, experience and training requirements for certain employees, the conduct of investment banking and research activities and the manner in which we prevent and detect money-laundering activities. Legislation and changes in rules promulgated by the SEC and by self-regulatory organizations or changes in the interpretation or enforcement of existing laws and rules often directly affect the method of operation and profitability of broker/dealers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The SEC, self-regulatory organizations and states may conduct administrative and enforcement proceedings that can result in censure, fine, suspension or revocation of a broker/dealer firm, its officers or employees.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our broker/dealer subsidiaries are subject to the SEC&#x2019;s net capital rule (Exchange Act Rule 15c3-1).&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, a broker/dealer&#x2019;s net capital is equal to its net worth plus qualified subordinated debt less deductions for non-allowable (or non-liquid) assets and other adjustments and operational charges.&nbsp;&nbsp;The SEC and FINRA impose rules that require notification when net capital falls below a certain threshold.&nbsp;&nbsp;These rules also dictate the ratio of debt-to-equity in the regulatory capital composition of a broker/dealer and constrain the ability of a broker/dealer to expand its business under certain circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;If a firm fails to maintain the required net capital, it may be subject to suspension or revocation of registration by the applicable regulatory authority, and suspension or revocation by these regulators could ultimately lead to the firm&#x2019;s liquidation.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Compliance with the net capital requirements may limit our operations, requiring the intensive use of capital. Such rules require that a certain percentage of our assets be maintained in relatively liquid form and therefore act to restrict our ability to withdraw capital from our broker/dealer subsidiaries, which in turn may limit our ability to pay dividends, repay debt or redeem or purchase shares of our outstanding common stock. Any change in such rules or the imposition of new rules affecting the scope, coverage, calculation or amount of capital requirements, or a significant operating loss or any unusually large charge against capital, could adversely affect our ability to pay dividends, meet our debt covenant requirements or to expand or maintain our operations. In addition, such rules may require us to make substantial capital contributions into one or more of our broker/dealer subsidiaries in order for such subsidiaries to comply with such rules, either in the form of cash or subordinated loans made in accordance with the requirements of the SEC&#x2019;s net capital rule. As of June 30, 2013, Southwest Securities had regulatory net capital, as defined by Exchange Act Rule 15c3-1, of $141.1 million, which exceeded the amounts required by $134.3 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As of June 30, 2013, SWS Financial had regulatory net capital, as defined by Exchange Act Rule 15c3-1, of $713,000, which exceeded the amounts required by $463,000.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the amount of net excess capital can change dramatically within a short period of time due to a variety of factors.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our broker/dealer subsidiaries are required by federal law to belong to the SIPC, whose primary function is to provide financial protection for the customers of failing brokerage firms.&nbsp;&nbsp;SIPC provides protection for clients&#x2019; cash and securities up to $500,000 per customer account, of which a maximum of $250,000 may be in cash.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Southwest Securities and SWS Financial are registered with, and subject to oversight and inspection by, the SEC as investment advisers under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended.&nbsp;&nbsp;The investment advisory business of our subsidiaries is subject to significant federal regulation, including with respect to wrap fee programs, the management of client accounts, the safeguarding of client assets, client fees and disclosures, transactions among affiliates and recordkeeping and reporting procedures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Legislation and changes in regulations promulgated by the SEC or changes in the interpretation or enforcement of existing laws and regulations often directly affect the method of operation and profitability of investment advisers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The SEC may conduct administrative and enforcement proceedings that can result in censure, fine, suspension, revocation or expulsion of an investment advisory firm, its officers or employees.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Certain activities of some SWS subsidiaries are regulated by the CFTC and various commodity exchanges. Southwest Securities and SWS Financial are registered as introducing brokers with the CFTC and NFA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The CFTC also has net capital regulations (CFTC Rule 1.17) that must be satisfied. Our futures business is also regulated by the NFA, a registered futures association. Violation of the rules of the CFTC, the NFA or the commodity exchanges could result in remedial actions including fines, registration restrictions or terminations, trading prohibitions or revocations of commodity exchange memberships.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Banking Regulations</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We are subject to the extensive regulatory framework applicable to savings and loan holding companies as well as federal savings associations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:10.8pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:left;font-family:Times New Roman;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">As a savings and loan holding company, we are subject to regulation and examination by the FRB. The Bank is subject to regulation and examination by the OCC (its primary federal regulator).&nbsp;&nbsp;The banking regulators,&nbsp;&nbsp;including the OCC, FDIC and FRB have broad and, in some cases, overlapping, authority to prohibit activities of holding companies, federal savings banks, their non-banking subsidiaries, directors, officers and other institution affiliated parties (such as attorneys and accountants) that represent unsafe and unsound banking practices or that constitute violations of laws or regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The OCC can assess civil money penalties for violations of law, certain orders, written conditions or written agreements with the OCC, as well as certain knowing and reckless activities, if those activities caused a substantial loss to a depository institution.&nbsp;&nbsp;The penalties can be as high as $1.375 million for each day the activities continue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Dodd-Frank Act transferred the functions of the OTS (other than consumer protection) as they relate to the Bank to the OCC, and as they relate to SWS Group, to the FRB on July 21, 2011 (&#x201C;Transfer Date&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Eventually, we will be required to comply with capital and activity requirements similar to those currently applicable to bank holding companies.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Dodd-Frank Act enacted new minimum capital requirements for depository institution holding companies and federal banking agencies have approved final rules implementing these statutory provisions for reporting periods after January 1, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The OCC published a final rule on the Transfer Date clarifying the application of its rules to federal savings banks in certain areas, including assessments, preemption of state law, visitorial powers and other clarifying administrative matters.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Dodd-Frank Act also requires the FRB to mandate that any bank holding company or savings and loan holding company serve as a &#x201C;source of strength&#x201D; for any subsidiary that is a depository institution.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Dodd-Frank Act gave the federal banking agencies one year after the Transfer Date to issue joint final rules related to the &#x201C;source of strength&#x201D; requirement, however, these rules have not been proposed.&nbsp;&nbsp;&#x201C;Source of strength&#x201D; is defined as the ability of a company that directly or indirectly owns or controls an insured depository institution to provide financial assistance to such insured depository institution in the event of the financial distress of the insured depository institution.&nbsp;&nbsp;Once these rules are finalized,&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS Group will be required to be a &#x201C;source of strength&#x201D; for the Bank.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In July 2010, the FDIC voted to revise its existing Memorandum of Understanding with the primary federal regulators to enhance the FDIC&#x2019;s existing authority over insured depository institutions that the FDIC does not directly supervise. As a result, the Bank may be subject to increased supervision by the FDIC.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">With very limited exceptions, we may not be acquired by any company or by any individual without the approval of a governing bank regulatory agency.&nbsp;&nbsp;That agency must complete an application review, and generally the public must have an opportunity to comment on any proposed acquisition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Without prior approval from the FRB, we may not acquire more than five percent of the voting stock of any savings institution or bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Dodd-Frank Act restricts a bank that is the subject of a formal enforcement action or a memorandum of understanding with respect to a significant supervisory matter from converting its charter, subject to certain exceptions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank is currently subject to OCC capital requirements. Federal statutes and OCC regulations have established four ratios for measuring an institution&#x2019;s capital adequacy: a &#x201C;Tier I (core) capital&#x201D; ratio&nbsp;&#x2014; the ratio of an institution&#x2019;s Tier&nbsp;I capital to </font>
