		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Business Environment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Performance in the financial services industry in which we operate is highly correlated to the overall strength of the economy and financial market activity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Overall market conditions are a product of many factors, which are beyond our control and can be unpredictable.&nbsp;&nbsp;These factors may affect the financial decisions made by investors, including their level of participation in the financial markets, which may in turn, affect our business results.&nbsp;&nbsp;With respect to financial market activity, our profitability is sensitive to a variety of factors, including the volatility of the equity and fixed income markets, the level and shape of various yield curves, the volume of trading in securities, the value of our customers&#x2019; assets under management, the demand for loans, the value of real estate in our market areas and the current political environment.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">As of June 30, 2013, equity market indices were up versus a year ago with the Dow Jones Industrial Average (the &#x201C;DJIA&#x201D;) up 15.8%, the Standard &amp; Poor&#x2019;s 500 Index (&#x201C;S&amp;P 500&#x201D;) up 12.2% and the NASDAQ Composite Index (&#x201C;NASDAQ&#x201D;) up 16.0%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The DJIA closed at 14,909.60 on June 28, 2013 up from 12,880.09 and 11,934.58 on June 29, 2012 and June 24, 2011, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;While the indexes showed improvement and reached closing prices that have not been reached since 2008, the average daily trading volume on the NYSE decreased 22% as compared to the same period of our prior fiscal year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The continued uncertainty in the economic environment both domestically and in Europe and continued high unemployment rates, contributed to volatility during our fiscal 2013.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Continued economic and regulatory uncertainty also created a challenging operating environment for us in fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The national unemployment rate, which was approximately 7.6% at the end of June 2013, was down from a high of 10.0% at the end of December 2009, and 8.2% at the end of June 2012, but remains at historically high levels.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The FRB reduced the federal funds target rate to 0 - 0.25% on December 16, 2008 and announced in January 2013 that it anticipated that rates were unlikely to increase as long as the unemployment rate remained above 6.5%, the short-term inflation rate was projected to be no more than 0.5% above the Federal Open Market Committee&#x2019;s 2% longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations continue to be stable. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The disruptions and developments in the world economy and the credit markets over the past three years resulted in a range of actions by the U.S. and foreign governments to attempt to bring liquidity and order to the financial markets and to prevent a long recession in the world economy. For more details regarding some of the actions taken by U.S. and foreign governments, see the discussion under Item 1. &#x201C;Business-Regulation.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Government intervention in the markets for the past several years has created artificially low short-term interest rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Public announcements by the FRB regarding timing of reduced intervention or increased interest rates has led to substantial volatility in the fixed income markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;This volatility has produced and could continue to produce material changes in the value of our fixed income trading portfolio.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Texas, along with the rest of the country, experienced distress in residential and commercial real estate values as well as elevated unemployment rates beginning in the last calendar quarter of 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;Real estate values, along with unemployment statistics, have improved in fiscal 2013; however, with the improvement, competition in the banking business has increased as loan demand is not yet robust.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Impact of Economic Environment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Brokerage:</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Volatility in the U.S. credit and mortgage markets, low interest rates and reduced volume in the U.S. stock markets continue to have an adverse effect on several aspects of our brokerage business, including depressed net interest margins, reduced liquidity and lower trading volumes. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font>
		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent: -10.1pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Exposure to European Sovereign Debt</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We have no exposure to European sovereign debt or direct exposure to European banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, we do participate in securities lending with U.S. subsidiaries of several European banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;Receivables from securities lending are secured by collateral equal to 102% of the market value of the underlying securities, and the collateral is adjusted daily to maintain the 102% margin.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent: -10.1pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent: -10.1pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Net Interest Margins</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Historically, the profitability of our brokerage business has been highly dependent upon net interest income.&nbsp;&nbsp;We earn net interest income on the spread between the interest rates earned and paid on customer and correspondent balances as well as from our securities lending business.&nbsp;&nbsp;With interest rates at historically low levels, the spread we are able to earn has been reduced, primarily from the extremely low yields on our portfolio of assets segregated for regulatory purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the spread in our securities lending business has declined.&nbsp;&nbsp;Lastly, because the yields on money market funds have declined significantly, revenue sharing arrangements with our primary money market fund providers have been substantially reduced.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not expect any significant changes in these dynamics until short-term interest rates rise.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We have taken actions to mitigate the impact of this margin contraction by renegotiating arrangements with our clearing customers, changing the mix of our assets segregated for regulatory purposes and developing new business in our securities lending portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;Despite these actions, profits from net interest remain substantially below historical levels.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent: -10.1pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:-1.1pt;width:10pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Liquidity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -2.9pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> Dislocation in the credit markets has led to increased liquidity risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;All but $45.0 million of our borrowing arrangements are uncommitted lines of credit and, as such, can be reduced or eliminated at any time by the lenders extending the credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we have not experienced any reductions in our uncommitted borrowing capacity, over the past three years, our lenders have taken actions that indicate their concerns regarding liquidity in the marketplace.&nbsp;&nbsp;These actions included reduced advance rates for certain security types, more stringent requirements for collateral eligibility, higher interest rates and pre-funding of daily settlements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Should our lenders&nbsp;&nbsp;take any actions that could negatively impact the terms of our lending arrangements, the cost of conducting our business would increase and our volume of business would be limited.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -2.9pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> The volatility in the U.S. stock markets has also impacted our liquidity through increased margin requirements at our clearing houses.&nbsp;&nbsp;These margin requirements are determined by the clearing houses through a combination of risk formulas that are periodically adjusted to reflect perceived risk in the market.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent we are required to post cash or other collateral to meet these requirements, we will have less liquidity to finance our other business.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect these margin requirements to continue to increase over the next 12 months.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -2.9pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Valuation of Securities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We trade mortgage, asset-backed and other types of fixed income securities on a regular basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;We monitor our trading limits daily to ensure that these securities are maintained at levels we consider prudent given current market conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;We price these securities using a third-party pricing service and we review the prices monthly to ensure reasonable valuations.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013, we held mortgage and asset-backed securities of approximately $38.3 million included in securities owned, at fair value on the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Bank:</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Shortly after closing the Hilltop and Oak Hill transaction, we contributed $20.0 million in capital to the Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe the $20.0 million capital contribution and access to additional capital from SWS Group provides the Bank with a sound foundation for future earnings, as well as the flexibility to accelerate the reduction of classified assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank continued to reduce classified assets during fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Classified assets were $67.6 million at June 30, 2013, down from $110.7 million at June 30, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Classified assets as a percentage of total capital plus the allowance for loan losses was 37.4% at June 30, 2013 and 58.0% at June 30, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Non-performing assets (a subset of classified assets) decreased to $38.0 million at June 30, 2013 from $72.7 million at June 30, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank has significantly reduced classified assets and improved performance during the past fiscal year, but the reduction in classified assets could slow and additional loans could be moved to problem status should the economic environment worsen.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank&#x2019;s loan loss allowance at June 30, 2013 was $12.3 million, or 2.85% of loans held for investment, excluding purchased mortgage loans held for investment and loans measured at fair value, as compared to $22.4 million, or 3.99% of loans held for investment, excluding purchased mortgage loans held for investment, at June 30, 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Tier I (core) capital ratio was 13.5% and the total risk-based capital ratio was 24.9% at June 30, 2013, as compared to 12.6% and 19.2%, respectively, at June 30, 2012 (without giving effect to the Basel III final rules).&nbsp;&nbsp;With the stability of these capital ratios and the $20.0 million capital contribution from SWS Group, the Bank&#x2019;s management has focused on diversifying the balance sheet by reducing loan concentrations and building an investment portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;In conjunction with building the security investment portfolio, the Bank entered into $100.0 million of interest rate swaps, to reduce deposit cost variability by focusing on </font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank is focused on implementing and executing its business plan, which includes the continued diversification of the balance sheet and conservative growth strategies. The Bank&#x2019;s available for sale investment portfolio was $503.1 million and $304.0 million at June 30, 2013 and June 30, 2012, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank plans to continue to manage a tiered investment portfolio designed to provide cash flows for loan originations.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and June 30, 2012, the Bank&#x2019;s mortgage purchase program loan balance was $174.0 million and $294.3 million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;These loans are held for investment on average for 25 days or less, which substantially limits credit risk.&nbsp; </font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The primary funding source for the Bank&#x2019;s balance sheet growth is core deposits from Southwest Securities&#x2019; brokerage customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;These core deposits provide the Bank with a stable and low cost funding source.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and June 30, 2012, the Bank had $878.4 million and $930.7 million, respectively, in funds on deposit from customers of Southwest Securities, representing approximately 88.4% and 87.6%, respectively, of the Bank&#x2019;s total deposits.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Deferred tax asset valuation allowance.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Deferred tax assets derived from operating losses are realized when we generate consolidated taxable income within the applicable carryback and carryforward periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on an evaluation of our historical results of operations and various other factors, management determined that it was appropriate to increase the valuation allowance for its remaining deferred tax assets with the exception of the Bank&#x2019;s available for sale securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management determined that an increase in the valuation allowance was appropriate in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2013 after reviewing the impact of our fourth quarter operating results and our fiscal 2014 financial forecast.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, we increased our valuation allowance by $30.0 million from $872,000 at June 29, 2012 to $30.9 million at June 30, 2013.&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Warrant valuation.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The warrants issued to Hilltop and Oak Hill are presented as liabilities carried at fair value on the Consolidated Statement of Financial Condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2013, the value of these warrants decreased primarily due to the decrease in the derived volatility of our common stock from 52% at June 30, 2012 to 51% at June 30, 2013 and the effect of the time to maturity.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in value resulted in an unrealized pre-tax gain of $3.6 million for fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2012, the value of these warrants increased due to increased stock price volatility from our initial valuation of 39.9% to 52.4%, partially offset by the passage of time and a decrease in our stock price from $5.45 at July 29, 2011, the issuance date of the warrants, to $5.33 at June 29, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in value resulted in an unrealized pre-tax loss of $3.7 million for fiscal 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Courier New;font-size: 9pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2013 versus 2012</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net revenues decreased $21.8 million from fiscal 2012 to fiscal 2013. The largest components of the decrease were a $10.7 million decrease in net gains on principal transactions, a $10.9 million decrease in net interest and a $6.2 million decrease in commissions, offset by a $4.4 million increase in investment banking, advisory and administrative fees and $2.3 million increase in other revenue.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $10.7 million decrease in net gains on principal transactions was primarily driven by a $14.7 million decrease in our institutional segment, with $12.5 million coming from our municipal distribution business and $2.3 million from our taxable fixed income business as a result of the market environment during the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;These decreases were offset by the $3.6 million realized gain on the sale of our shares of U.S. Home Systems, Inc. (&#x201C;USHS&#x201D;) common stock.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> &nbsp; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The $10.9 million decrease in net interest revenue was primarily driven by a $5.8 million decrease in net interest revenue in our banking segment due to a 21% decrease in our average loan balance and a 30 basis point decrease in net interest yield at the Bank as compared to the same period of the prior fiscal year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The institutional segment contributed an additional $3.2 million of the net interest revenue decrease primarily due to a 12 basis point decrease in our average net interest spread in our stock lending business and an 8% decrease in our average stock lending portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense under the Credit Agreement contributed $1.5 million of the decrease in net interest revenue as there was one month less of interest expense for fiscal 2012.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The $6.2 million decrease in commissions revenue from fiscal 2012 to fiscal 2013 was due to a $4.7 million decrease in the institutional segment and a $1.5 million decrease in commissions in the retail segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both decreases were due in part to a decrease in the number of trading days from 256 days in fiscal year 2012 to 249 days in fiscal year 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in commissions in the retail segment was also due to the loss of a team of high performing independent registered representative producers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in commissions in the institutional segment was also due to the narrowing of bid/ask spreads and an increase in market volatility in the last half of the year.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The $4.4 million increase in investment banking and advisory fees was primarily due to a 43% increase in our assets under management and an increase in administrative fee income from revenue sharing with money market fund providers in our clearing and retail segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The $2.3 million increase in other revenues was primarily a result of a $1.7 million increase in the sale of insurance products in our retail segment, a $1.3 million increase in the value of our deferred compensation investments and a $2.3 million increase in gains on the sale of loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;These increases were partially offset by a $1.0 million increase in net losses on the sale of real estate owned (&#x201C;REO&#x201D;) and a $0.4 million decrease in the gains from sale of securities.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses decreased $21.0 million in fiscal year 2013 as compared to the same period of the prior fiscal year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The largest components of this decrease were a $10.2 million decrease in our provision for loan loss, a $7.3 million decrease in the change in the value of the warrants, a $2.1 million decrease in other expenses and a $1.4 million decrease in commissions and other employee compensation expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;We recognized a loan loss recapture of $7.7 million for fiscal year 2013 compared to a provision of $2.5 million for fiscal year 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;We recognized a $3.6 million gain on the warrant valuation in fiscal year 2013 and a $3.7 million loss on the warrant valuation in fiscal year 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $2.1 million decrease in other expenses in fiscal 2013 was primarily due to a $1.7 million decrease in legal fees from fiscal year 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The $1.4 million decrease in commissions and other employee compensation was primarily due to overall segment revenue declines leading to a decrease in commission expense and incentive compensation of $8.9 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;These decreases were partially offset by an increase in our liability to participants in the deferred compensation plan of $1.4 million and salary and benefit expenses of $6.1 million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2012 versus 2011</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net revenues decreased $48.6 million from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The largest components of the decrease were a $29.3 million decrease in net interest, a $10.8 million decrease in commissions, a $9.2 million decrease in net gains on principal transactions and a $1.3 million decrease in net revenues from clearing operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $29.3 million decrease in net interest revenue was due primarily to a 27% decrease in the average loan balance at the Bank compared to fiscal 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, interest expense under the Credit Agreement with Hilltop and Oak Hill reduced net interest revenue by $11.0 million for fiscal 2012.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The decrease in commissions was due primarily to a $6.7 million decrease in commissions in the institutional segment, primarily in the taxable fixed income business resulting from reduced customer activity due to increased economic uncertainty.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we also experienced a $4.1 million decrease in commissions in the retail segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was primarily due to a decrease in retail representative headcount, difficulty in recruiting representatives and reduced activity overall.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The $9.2 million decrease in net gains on principal transactions was due to reduced customer trading activity in the taxable fixed income and municipal finance businesses.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The decrease in net revenues from clearing operations was due </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">primarily to changes in market conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the loss of 12 correspondents to broker withdrawals in fiscal 2012 also contributed to the decrease in clearing revenue. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">These revenue declines were partially offset by a $2.4 million increase in other revenue.&nbsp;&nbsp;This increase was made up of a $3.1 million decrease in net losses on the sale of REO from the prior fiscal year, a $0.8 million increase in earnings on equity investments, a $0.6 million increase in insurance product sales and a $0.5 million decrease on losses on the sale of loans offset by a $1.6 million decrease in the value of the investments in our deferred compensation plan and a $0.6 million decrease in the gain on sale of securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses decreased $76.2 million for fiscal 2012 as compared to fiscal 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;The largest decreases were the $48.5 million decrease in the provision for loan loss, the $17.0 million decrease in other expense, the $11.8 million decrease in commissions and other employee compensation and the $2.2 million decrease in occupancy, equipment and computer service costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in the Bank&#x2019;s loan loss provision is discussed above under &#x201C;Overview-Business Environment-Impact of Economic Environment-Bank.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in other expenses was due primarily to a $13.0 million decrease in the Bank&#x2019;s REO loss provision, a $1.4 million decrease in third-party loan services, a $1.1 million decrease in the Bank&#x2019;s fee assessments from </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Periodic reviews of the carrying amount of deferred tax assets are made to determine if the establishment of a valuation allowance is necessary when it is more likely than not that all or a portion of a deferred tax asset will not be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;In </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">assessing the realization of deferred tax assets, management considered all available evidence, both positive and negative from the following expected sources of income:&nbsp;&nbsp;expected future reversals of deferred tax assets and liabilities, projected future taxable income, cumulative losses in recent years and tax planning strategies. In making such judgments, significant weight is given to evidence that can be objectively verified.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC") 740, &#x201C;Income Taxes&#x201D; provides that a cumulative loss in recent years is significant negative evidence in considering whether deferred tax assets are realizable and also restricts the reliance on projections of future taxable income to support the recovery of deferred tax assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although our current financial forecasts indicate that sufficient taxable income should be generated in the future to ultimately realize the existing deferred tax benefits, these forecasts are subject to a number of assumptions and there can be no assurance that these forecasts will be achieved.&nbsp;&nbsp;These forecasts were not considered to constitute sufficient positive evidence, as required by GAAP, to overcome the observable negative evidence associated with the cumulative loss positions. The company previously had an allowance for deferred tax assets associated with its capital losses from investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on an evaluation of the positive and negative evidence, management determined that it was appropriate to increase the valuation allowance for its remaining deferred tax assets, except for the Bank&#x2019;s available for sale securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;See also </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 17</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2013, June 29, 2012 and June 24, 2011 included under Item 8. &#x201C;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.&#x201D;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:8pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2013 versus 2012</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">For fiscal 2013, net revenues in the clearing segment increased 2% while clearing fee revenues decreased 7% and other revenues increased 31% compared to fiscal year 2012.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The $0.7 million decrease in clearing revenue was primarily due to lower activity levels for existing correspondents and a decrease from 256 trading days in fiscal year 2012 to 249 trading days in fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in clearing fee revenues was offset by an increase in other revenues primarily due to a $0.5 million increase in revenue sharing with money market fund providers and increased earnings on customer assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">For fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012, tickets processed for high-volume trading firms decreased 66% while tickets processed for general securities broker/dealers decreased by 10%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue per ticket increased approximately 60% from $5.61 for fiscal 2012 to $8.99 for fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The change in the mix of tickets processed led to an increase in revenue per ticket as fees charged to high-volume trading firms are discounted substantially from the fees charged to general securities broker/dealers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses for fiscal 2013 decreased $0.9 million, or 5%, from fiscal 2012 primarily due to a decrease in operations and information technology expenses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2012 versus 2011</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">-</font><font style="display: inline;">40</font><font style="display: inline;">-</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 8pt">

			<a href="#IndexToAnnualReport"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:8pt;">Table Of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">For fiscal 2012, net revenues and clearing fee revenue in the clearing segment both decreased 12% from fiscal 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, other revenue decreased 21% from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012 primarily due to a 25% decline in administrative fee income from revenue sharing with money market fund providers.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The decrease in clearing revenue was due primarily to changes in market conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the loss of 12 correspondents to broker withdrawals in fiscal 2012 also contributed to the decrease in clearing revenue.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Also, for fiscal 2012 as compared to fiscal 2011, tickets processed for high-volume trading firms decreased 38% while tickets processed for general securities broker/dealers decreased by 8%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue per ticket increased approximately 29% from $4.35 for fiscal 2011 to $5.61 for fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The change in the mix of tickets processed led to an increase in revenue per ticket as fees charged to high-volume trading firms are discounted substantially from the fees charged to general securities broker/dealers.&nbsp;&nbsp;A four day increase in the number of trading days in fiscal 2012 compared to the prior fiscal year partially offset the decrease in ticket volume.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were 256 trading days in fiscal 2012 and 252 in fiscal 2011.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses for fiscal 2012 decreased $0.3 million, or 2%, from fiscal 2011 due primarily to a $0.4 million decrease in occupancy, equipment and computer service costs, primarily due to a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$0.8 million decrease in amortization expense related to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">a customer relationship intangible that was fully amortized in July 2011</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was offset by a $0.3 million increase in information technology costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2013 versus 2012</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net revenues in the retail segment increased 3% in fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012 despite the seven fewer trading days during the fiscal 2013 period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Advisory fees were up in all areas of the retail business due to a 43% increase in assets under management as well as increased fees from money market fund revenue sharing.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, insurance products revenue was up 12% from the prior year period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commission revenues increased 6% in our PCG group while representative turnover resulted in an overall 15% reduction in commissions revenue at SWS Financial.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Total customer assets were $14.3 billion at June 30, 2013 and $13.6 billion at June 29, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets under management were $1.1 billion at June 30, 2013 versus $761.1 million at June 29, 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses decreased 1% from fiscal 2012 to fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was primarily due to a $2.5 million decrease in legal expenses offset by a $1.1 million increase in commissions and other employee compensation primarily at our PCG group.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2012 versus 2011</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net revenues in the retail segment decreased 3% in fiscal 2012 as compared to fiscal 2011 due primarily to a $4.1 million decrease in commissions resulting from a reduction in PCG representative headcount in fiscal 2011, with the bulk of the reduction coming in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;The average PCG representative headcount for fiscal 2011 was 184 representatives compared to 166 in fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in net revenues can also be attributed to reduced activity overall.&nbsp;&nbsp;Despite these challenges, insurance product sales for fiscal 2012 increased from fiscal 2011 due to improved volumes in both our PCG and SWS Financial businesses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Total customer assets were $13.6 billion at June 29, 2012 and $12.9 billion at June 24, 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets under management were $761.1 million at June 29, 2012 versus $688.5 million at June 24, 2011. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses increased less than 1% from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, other expenses increased 10% from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in other expenses was primarily due to a $0.9 million increase in legal fees and a $0.4 million increase in operational and information technology costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;This increase in other expenses was offset by a decrease in occupancy, equipment and computer service costs of $0.6 million, which was due to the completion of an M.L. Stern &amp; Co., LLC computer services contract in early fiscal 2012.</font>
		</p>

						<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">2011</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:04.08%;height:15pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;text-align:right;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
						&nbsp;</p>
				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:34.44%;height:15pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">572</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:04.08%;height:15pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
						&nbsp;</p>
				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:28.42%;height:15pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0.05pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;47,467,640,000</font></p>
				</td>
			</tr>
		</table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2013 versus 2012</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net revenues from the institutional segment decreased 17% while pre-tax income was down 47% from fiscal 2012 to fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was due primarily to a $14.7 million decrease in net gains on principal transactions, a $4.7 million decrease in commission revenues and a $3.2 million decrease in net interest revenue.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in net gains on principal transactions was primarily due to a $12.5 million decrease in municipal finance trading gains and a $2.3 million decrease in taxable fixed income gains.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in both the taxable fixed income and municipal finance trading gains was primarily the result of the challenging market environment in the later half of fiscal 2013, particularly in the fourth quarter in which municipal and taxable yields increased significantly and the yield on the 10-year treasury note increased by approximately 65 basis points from April 2013 to June 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;This dramatic rise in rates resulted in corresponding trading losses in our fourth fiscal quarter of 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The decrease in commission revenues was primarily driven by a $3.4 million decrease in taxable fixed income and a $1.6 million decrease in municipal finance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decreases in taxable fixed income and municipal finance were primarily attributable to the narrowing of bid/ask spreads and an increase in market volatility.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net interest revenue decreased $3.2 million for fiscal 2013 as compared to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease in net interest revenue was primarily due to a 12 basis point decrease in the average net interest spread in our stock loan business and a 6% reduction in average stock borrow balances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other net interest decreased $0.6 million for fiscal year 2013 primarily due to an increase in borrowing costs for our municipal and taxable fixed income businesses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses decreased 4% for fiscal 2013 as compared to fiscal 2012, primarily due to a $6.6 million decrease in compensation expenses due to weaker segment revenues offset by a $1.1 million increase in quotations and a $0.9 million increase in operations and technology expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2012 versus 2011</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net revenues from the institutional segment decreased 11% while pre-tax income was down 14% from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commissions decreased $6.7 million from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012 due to reduced customer activity, primarily in the taxable fixed income business</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> due to increased economic uncertainty</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;These decreases for fiscal 2012 were partially offset by a 19% increase in portfolio trading commissions due to increased customer activity and a one time change in customer business mix.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net gains on principal transactions decreased $8.2 million, or 22%, in fiscal 2012 as compared to fiscal 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;Taxable fixed income trading gains decreased $3.6 million and municipal finance trading gains decreased $5.2 million from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses decreased 9% for fiscal 2012 compared to fiscal 2011, primarily due to decreased commissions and other employee compensation from reduced revenue produced by the institutional segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2013 versus 2012</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">For fiscal year 2013, the Bank&#x2019;s net revenues decreased 12% compared to fiscal 2012 due primarily to a $5.8 million reduction in net interest.&nbsp;&nbsp;This reduction in net interest was primarily due to the 21% decrease in average loan balances, as well as a 30 basis point decrease in the net yield on interest-earning assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The reduction in net interest yield was due to the roll off of the held for investment loan portfolio with proceeds being invested in the Bank&#x2019;s investment portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;This portfolio is weighted to provide liquidity as the Bank begins to record net loan originations.&nbsp;&nbsp;For the 2013 fiscal year-to-date, the Bank had originations of $5.6 billion and repayments on loans of $5.8 billion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank&#x2019;s operating expenses decreased $11.3 million, or 26%, for fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012 and was primarily attributable to the $10.2 million decrease in the provision for loan losses as the Bank recorded $2.5 million in provision expense for fiscal 2012 compared to a $7.7 million loan loss recapture for fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other operating expenses decreased $1.1 million for fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was due primarily to a $0.8 million decrease in legal expenses, a $0.7 million decrease in REO related expenses and a $0.5 million decrease in regulatory fees.&nbsp;&nbsp;These decreases were offset by a $1.4 million increase in commission and other employee compensation and a $0.5 million increase in the REO loss provision.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2012 versus 2011</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">For fiscal 2012 as compared to fiscal 2011, the Bank&#x2019;s net revenues decreased 22%, but the Bank posted pre-tax income of $7.3 million, up from a pre-tax loss of $46.3 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in net interest revenue at the Bank for fiscal 2012 as compared to the prior fiscal year was due primarily to a 27% decrease in average loan balances, as well as a decrease in the net yield on interest-earning assets of 70 basis points.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other revenue increased $3.6 million for fiscal 2012 as compared to the prior fiscal year.&nbsp;&nbsp;This increase was primarily due to a $3.1 million decrease in net losses on the sale of REO, a $1.2 million increase in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">earnings on equity investments</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and a $0.5 million net decrease in losses on the sale of loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;These increases were offset by a decrease on the gain of sale of securities of $0.6 million and a $0.5 million decrease in miscellaneous revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:36pt;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Bank&#x2019;s operating expenses decreased 61% for fiscal 2012 compared to fiscal 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;This decrease was due primarily to a $48.5 million decrease in the Bank&#x2019;s loan loss provision and a $17.1 million decrease in other expenses, which included the following:&nbsp;&nbsp;(i) a $13.0 million decrease in the Bank&#x2019;s REO loss provision; (ii) a $1.4 million decrease in third-party loan review services; (iii) a $1.1 million decrease in the Bank&#x2019;s fee assessments from regulatory agencies; (iv) a $0.7 million decrease in real estate related and other loan related expense and (v) a $0.2 million decrease in legal expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in the Bank&#x2019;s loan loss provision was due to greater stability in the rate of decline of commercial real estate values and a reduction in size of the Bank&#x2019;s loan portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance computation is discussed in detail under &#x201C;-Financial Condition-Loans and Allowance for Probable Loan Loss&#x201D; below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Other.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The following discusses the financial results for SWS Group, corporate administration and SWS Capital Corporation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2013 versus 2012</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Pre-tax loss from the other segment was $42.3 million for fiscal year 2013 compared to a pre-tax loss of $49.3 million for fiscal year 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The primary driver of the $7.0 million decrease in the pre-tax loss was related to the recognition of a $3.6 million unrealized gain on the valuation of the warrants held by Hilltop and Oakhill for the fiscal year 2013 compared to a $3.7 million unrealized loss on the valuation for the warrants held by Hilltop and Oak Hill for the fiscal year 2012.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net revenues increased $2.3 million for fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in net revenues was primarily due to the $3.6 million gain recognized from our sale of USHS shares in addition to a $1.3 million increase in the value of our deferred compensation plan&#x2019;s investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;These increases were partially offset by a $0.7 million write down in fair value of an auction rate municipal bond and a $1.5 million increase in interest expense related to the outstanding borrowings under the Credit Agreement with Hilltop and Oak Hill in fiscal 2013 compared to fiscal 2012 which included one less month of interest expense</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Operating expenses increased $2.7 million for the fiscal year 2013 as compared to the fiscal year 2012 primarily due to a $1.4 million increase in the value of our deferred compensation plan&#x2019;s funds and a $1.2 million increase in legal expenses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Fiscal 2012 versus 2011</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Pre-tax loss from the other segment was $49.3 million for fiscal 2012 compared to $35.2 million for fiscal 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net revenues decreased $13.3 million in fiscal 2012 primarily due to a decline in net interest revenue of $10.9 million and a decrease in other revenue of $1.7 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decline in net interest revenue was due to the interest expense recorded related to the $100 million Credit Agreement with Hilltop and Oak Hill in fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decrease in other revenue was primarily due to a $1.6 million decrease in the value of our deferred compensation plan&#x2019;s investments and a $0.4 million decrease in earnings on our equity investment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating expenses remained flat during the year with a slight increase of $0.7 million from fiscal 2011 to fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;This increase included the $3.7 million unrealized loss in the value of the warrants issued to Hilltop and Oak Hill.&nbsp;&nbsp;The unrealized loss in the value of the warrants was offset by a $1.6 million decrease in the value of our deferred compensation plan&#x2019;s investments and a $1.6 million decrease in legal expenses.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Univers (W1);font-weight:bold;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">FINANCIAL CONDITION</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-weight:bold;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Investments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-weight:bold;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:normal;font-size:9pt;">In fiscal 2013, the Bank implemented an investment strategy to diversify its balance sheet, absorb excess liquidity, and maximize interest income through investment in a conservative securities portfolio. &nbsp;The securities portfolio is structured to provide cash flows that will mitigate interest rate risk and ensure adequate funds are available for new loan originations.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
