		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined by Rule 13a-15(f) and Rule 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our internal control over financial reporting is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;In making this assessment, we used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organization of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in Internal Control-Integrated 1992 Framework.&nbsp;&nbsp;A control system, no matter how well conceived, implemented and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the internal control system are met.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because of such inherent limitations, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues, if any, within a company have been detected.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on our assessment and those criteria, our management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of June 30, 2013. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Our independent registered public accounting firm has audited the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2013 as stated in their report, dated September 6, 2013, which appears herein.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(b) Use of Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#x201C;GAAP&#x201D;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(c) Cash and Cash Equivalents</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">For the purposes of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, SWS considers cash to include cash on hand and in bank accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, SWS considers funds due from banks and interest bearing deposits in other banks to be cash. Highly liquid debt instruments purchased with maturities of three months or less, when acquired, are considered to be cash equivalents.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#x201C;FDIC&#x201D;) insures deposit accounts up to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">250,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Until December 31, 2012,&nbsp;&nbsp;in accordance with the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the &#x201C;Dodd-Frank Act&#x201D;), non-interest bearing transaction accounts had unlimited coverage under FDIC insurance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Non-interest bearing transaction accounts no longer have unlimited coverage under FDIC insurance and are insured up to $250,000.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012, cash balances included $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">37,833,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">30,504,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">, respectively, that were not federally insured because they exceeded federal insurance limits.&nbsp;&nbsp;This at-risk amount is subject to fluctuation on a daily basis, but management does not believe there is significant risk on these deposits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The Bank is required to maintain </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">reserve </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">balances on hand or with the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and 2012, these reserve balances amounted to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">1,649,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">1,503,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(d) Restricted Cash and Cash Equivalents</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Restricted cash and cash equivalents represents funds received from Hilltop Holdings, Inc. (&#x201C;Hilltop&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> Oak Hill Capital Partners III, L.P. (&#x201C;OHCP&#x201D;) and Oak Hill Capital Management Partners III, L.P. (collectively with OHCP, &#x201C;Oak Hill&#x201D;) upon completion of the $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">100,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> unsecured loan from Hilltop and Oak Hill under the terms of a credit agreement that was entered into on July 29, 2011 (the &#x201C;Credit Agreement&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is required to keep these funds in a restricted account until the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors, Hilltop and Oak Hill determine the amount(s) to be distributed to the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;See additional discussion in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;">Note 16, Debt Issued with Stock Purchase Warrants</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon approval of the Board of Directors, Hilltop and Oak Hill, SWS Group contributed $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">20,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> of this cash in the second quarter of fiscal 2012 to the Bank as capital, loaned Southwest Securities $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">20,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> in the third quarter of fiscal 2012 to use in general operations by reducing Southwest Securities&#x2019; use of short-term borrowings for the financing of its day-to-day cash management needs, reduced its intercompany payable to Southwest Securities by $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">20,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> and contributed $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">10,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> in capital to Southwest Securities in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 28, 2013, the $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">20,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> loan from SWS Group to Southwest Securities was repaid and the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors, Hilltop and Oak Hill approved a $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">20,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> capital contribution to Southwest Securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The remaining $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">30,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> is held in a restricted account at SWS Group to be used for general corporate purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Restricted cash and cash equivalents are excluded from cash and cash equivalents in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition and Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company holds restricted cash and cash equivalents in money market funds.</font>
		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(e) Securities Transactions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Proprietary securities transactions are recorded on a trade date basis, as if they had settled.&nbsp;&nbsp;Clients&#x2019; securities and commodities transactions are reported on a settlement date basis with the related commission income and expenses reported on a trade date basis.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(f) Securities Lending Activities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Securities borrowed and securities loaned transactions are generally reported as collateralized financings except where letters of credit or other securities are used as collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Securities borrowed transactions require the Company to deposit cash, letters of credit, or other collateral with the lender.&nbsp;&nbsp;With respect to securities loaned, the Company receives collateral in the form of cash in an amount generally in excess of the fair value of securities loaned.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company monitors the fair value of securities borrowed and loaned on a daily basis, with additional collateral obtained or refunded as necessary.&nbsp;&nbsp;Securities borrowed and securities loaned transactions are recorded at the amount of cash collateral advanced or received adjusted for additional collateral obtained or received.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest on such transactions is accrued and included in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition in receivables from and payables to brokers, dealers and clearing organizations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;"> (g) Loans and Allowance for Loan Losses</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Loans that management has the intent and ability to hold for the foreseeable future or until maturity or pay-off are reported at their outstanding principal balance adjusted for any charge-offs, the allowance for probable loan losses, and any deferred fees or costs on originated loans and unamortized premiums or discounts on purchased loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest income is accrued on the unpaid principal balance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Loan origination and commitment fees and certain related direct costs are deferred and amortized to interest income, generally over the contractual lives of the loans, using the interest method.&nbsp;&nbsp;Discounts on first mortgage, consumer and other loans are amortized to income using the interest method over the remaining period to contractual maturity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The accrual of interest on impaired loans is discontinued when, in management&#x2019;s opinion, the borrower may be unable to meet payments as they become due.&nbsp;&nbsp;When interest accrual is discontinued, all unpaid accrued interest is reversed.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest income is subsequently recognized to the extent cash payments are received for loans where ultimate full collection is likely.&nbsp;&nbsp;For loans where ultimate collection is not likely, interest payments are applied to the outstanding principal and income is only recognized if full payment is made.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loans are returned to accrual status when all the principal and interest amounts contractually due are brought current and future payments are reasonably assured.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">Purchased Mortgage Loans Held for Investment. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> Loan participations and sub-participations in the Bank&#x2019;s mortgage purchase program are acquired from various mortgage companies and valued at amortized cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;These loans are pre-sold by the mortgage company to secondary investors who have been approved by the Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchased mortgage loans held for investment are held on average for 25 days or less.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">Loans Measured at Fair Value.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">As permitted by Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC") 825, &#x201C;Financial Instruments,&#x201D; the Bank has elected to measure certain loans at fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management has elected the fair value option for these items to offset the corresponding change in fair value of the related interest rate swap agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The change in fair value is recorded in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">other revenue on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Loss.&nbsp;&nbsp;For additional discussion regarding these loans and the related interest rate swaps, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">see </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;">Note 5, Loans and Allowance for Probable Loan Losses</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;">Note 11, Interest Rate Swaps</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">Allowance for Loan Losses.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> &nbsp;The allowance for loan losses is maintained to absorb management&#x2019;s estimate of probable loan losses inherent in the Bank&#x2019;s loan portfolio at each reporting date.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance for loan losses is established as losses are estimated to have occurred through a provision for loan losses charged to earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loan losses are charged against the allowance when management confirms the uncollectibility of the principal loan balance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent recoveries, if any, are recorded through the allowance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The determination of an adequate allowance is inherently subjective, as it requires estimates that are susceptible to significant revision as additional information becomes available or circumstances change.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The allowance for loan losses is evaluated on a regular basis by management and is based upon management&#x2019;s periodic review of the collectibility of the loans in light of historical experience, the nature and volume of the loan </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">9</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">portfolio, adverse situations that may affect the borrower&#x2019;s ability to repay, estimated value of any underlying collateral and prevailing economic conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance for loan losses consists of a specific and a general allowance component.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The specific allowance component provides for estimated probable losses for loans identified as impaired.&nbsp;&nbsp;A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Bank will be unable to collect all amounts of principal and interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management considers the borrower&#x2019;s financial condition, payment status, historical payment record, and any adverse situations affecting the borrower&#x2019;s ability to repay when evaluating whether a loan is deemed impaired.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loans that experience insignificant payment delays and shortfalls generally are not classified as impaired. Management determines the significance of payment delays and shortfalls on a case-by-case basis taking into consideration all circumstances surrounding the loan and the borrower, including the length of delay, the reasons for the delay, the borrower&#x2019;s prior payment record, and the amount of shortfall in relation to the principal and interest outstanding.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">A specific reserve is recorded when and to the extent the recorded value of the loan is greater than (1) the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#x2019;s original effective rate, (2) fair value of collateral if the loan is collateral-dependent or (3) observable market price of the impaired loan.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the fair value of collateral is used to measure impairment of a collateral-dependent loan and repayment is dependent on the sale of the collateral, the fair value is adjusted to incorporate estimated costs to sell the collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Impaired loans that are collateral-dependent are primarily measured for impairment using the fair value of the collateral as determined by third party appraisals using the income approach, recent comparable sales data, or a combination thereof.&nbsp;&nbsp;In certain instances it is necessary for management to adjust the appraised value, less estimated costs to sell the collateral, to reflect changes in fair value occurring subsequent to the appraisal date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management considers a guarantor&#x2019;s capacity and willingness to perform, when appropriate, and the borrower&#x2019;s resources available for repayment when measuring impairment.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The general allowance provides for estimated and probable losses inherent in the remainder of the Bank&#x2019;s loan portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The general allowance is determined through a statistical calculation based on the Bank's historical loss experience adjusted for certain qualitative factors as deemed appropriate by management.&nbsp;&nbsp;The statistical calculation is conducted on a disaggregated basis for groups of homogeneous loans with similar risk characteristics (product types).&nbsp;&nbsp;The historical loss element is calculated as the average ratio of charge-offs, net of recoveries, to the average recorded investment for the current and previous five quarters.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management may adjust the historical loss rates to reflect other circumstances, such as deterioration in the real estate market, significant concentrations of product types, trends in portfolio volume, and the credit quality of the loan portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, prevailing economic conditions and specific industry trends are taken into consideration when establishing the adjustments to historical loss rates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">Changes in the calculation of the Allowance for Loan Losses. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">For the years ended June 30, 2011 and 2012, due to accelerated deterioration in the Bank&#x2019;s loan portfolio, depressed appraised values for collateral, continued high unemployment rates in Texas and deteriorating banking industry loss statistics, the Bank&#x2019;s management reevaluated certain components of its computation of the allowance for loan losses as follows: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td align="left" valign="top" style="width: 36.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Courier New;font-size:10pt;"> o</font>
			</p>
		</td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">In the first quarter of fiscal 2011, management provided a separate calculation for the problem loan volume trend component for criticized and classified loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to the first quarter of fiscal 2011, the Bank had one calculation for these loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;To more appropriately assess the significant increase in classified loans, the Bank provided a heavier weighting for these types of loans in the Bank&#x2019;s allowance calculation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank segregated these loans and applied a historical loss ratio based on industry total charge-off levels applied to criticized and classified loans.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>

			</p>
		</td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">In fiscal 2012, the Bank enhanced its allowance for loan loss calculation to reflect the credit quality of the Bank&#x2019;s loan portfolio in the current economic environment.&nbsp; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">In the third quarter of fiscal 2013, due to an improvement in the Bank&#x2019;s loss history over the past four quarters, the Bank&#x2019;s management reevaluated certain components of its computation of the allowance for loan losses as follows:</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">For additional discussion regarding the calculation of the Company&#x2019;s allowance for probable loan losses see </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;">Note 5, Loans and Allowance for Probable Loan Losses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(h) Securities Owned</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Marketable securities are carried at fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase or decrease in net unrealized appreciation or depreciation of securities owned is credited or charged to operations and is included in net gains on principal transactions in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Loss.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS records the fair value of securities owned on a trade date basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;See </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;">Note 1(x) and Note 26, Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(i) Securities Held to Maturity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Bonds and notes for which the Company has the intent and ability to hold to maturity are reported at cost, adjusted for premiums and discounts that are recognized in interest income using the interest method over the period to maturity.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(j) Securities Purchased Under Agreements to Resell and Securities Sold Under Agreements to Repurchase</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Transactions involving purchases of securities under agreements to resell (reverse repurchase agreements or reverse repos) or sales of securities under agreements to repurchase (repurchase agreements or repos) are accounted for as collateralized financings except where the Company does not have an agreement to sell (or purchase) the same or substantially the same securities before maturity at a fixed or determinable price.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is the policy of the Company to obtain possession of collateral with a fair value equal to or in excess of the principal amount loaned under resale agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Collateral is valued daily, and the Company may require counterparties to deposit additional collateral or return collateral pledged when appropriate. Interest payable on these amounts is included in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition in other liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(k) Goodwill</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The Company implemented the concepts outlined in Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) 2011-08 regarding its annual goodwill assessment of fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ASU highlights that an entity is no longer required to calculate the fair value of a reporting unit unless the entity determines, based on a qualitative assessment, that it is more likely than not that a reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value is less than its carrying amount.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Based on the results of its assessment, SWS&#x2019;s goodwill balance was not impaired.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS based its assessment of the fair value of the business units with goodwill on a weighted average of a discounted cash flow model estimate of fair value and a market multiple approach to fair value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">SWS has two reporting units with goodwill: Clearing with $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">4,254,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> and Institutional Brokerage with $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">3,298,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">, both of which are part of Southwest Securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">no</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> changes in the carrying value of goodwill during the fiscal years ended June 30, 2013, June 29, 2012 and June 24, 2011.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(l) Investments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Limited partnership investments are accounted for under the equity method of accounting in accordance with ASC 323, &#x201C;Investments-Equity Method and Joint Ventures.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(m) Interest Rate Swaps in Cash Flow Hedging Relationships</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">The Bank recognizes interest rate swaps as either assets or liabilities in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">A portion of the Bank&#x2019;s investment in interest rate swaps are derivatives designated in cash flow hedging relationships.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank has formally documented the following in regard to these hedging relationships: (i) its risk management objective; (ii) the strategy used for undertaking the hedge; (iii) the hedging instrument; (iv) the hedged transaction; (iv) the nature of the risk being hedged; (v) how the hedging instrument&#x2019;s effectiveness in offsetting the hedged risk will be assessed prospectively and retrospectively and (vi)&nbsp;&nbsp;a description of the method used to measure ineffectiveness. The Bank has also formally assessed, both at the inception of the hedging </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(n) Real Estate Owned (&#x201C;REO&#x201D;) and Other Repossessed Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">REO and other repossessed assets are valued at the lower of cost or market, less a selling discount and are included in other assets in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;For those investments where the REO is valued at market, the value is determined by third party appraisals or if the REO is subject to a sales contract, by the accepted sales amount.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, under certain circumstances, the Bank adjusts appraised values to more accurately reflect the economic conditions of the area at the time of valuation or to reflect changes in market value occurring subsequent to the appraisal date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in other repossessed assets are land leases which are valued using a discounted cash flow analysis.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of subsequent write-downs required to reflect current fair value was $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">1,657,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">1,301,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">14,221,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> for fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;">(o) Fixed Assets and Depreciation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">Fixed assets are comprised of furniture, computer hardware, equipment and leasehold improvements and are included in other assets in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additions, improvements and expenditures for repairs and maintenance that significantly extend the useful life of an asset are capitalized.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other expenditures for repairs and maintenance are charged to expense in the period incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation of furniture and equipment is provided over the estimated useful lives of the assets (from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">three</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">seven</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> years), and depreciation on leasehold improvements is provided over the shorter of the useful life or the lease term (up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">fifteen</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> years) using the straight-line method.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation of buildings is provided over the useful life (up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">forty</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> years) using the straight-line method. Depreciation expense totaled approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">5,472,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">5,763,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">, and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">6,423,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> for fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Furniture, equipment and leasehold improvements are tested for potential impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances suggest that an asset&#x2019;s or asset group&#x2019;s carrying value may not be fully recoverable.&nbsp;&nbsp;An impairment loss, calculated as the difference between the estimated fair value and the carrying value of an asset or asset group, is recognized if the sum of the expected undiscounted cash flows relating to the asset or asset group is less than the corresponding carrying value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;"> (p) Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">An entity is defined as a variable interest entity (&#x201C;VIE&#x201D;) and subject to consolidation if:&nbsp;&nbsp;(1) the total equity investment at risk is not sufficient to permit the entity to finance its activities without additional subordinated financial support provided by any parties or (2) the holders of the equity investment at risk in the entity lack the ability to make significant decisions about the entity&#x2019;s operations or are not obligated to absorb the expected losses or receive the expected returns of the entity.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The reporting entity, if any, which has a controlling financial interest in a VIE is required to possess:&nbsp;&nbsp;(1) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact the VIE&#x2019;s economic performance and (2) the obligation to absorb potentially significant losses or the right to receive potentially significant benefits from the VIE.&nbsp;&nbsp;The entity which has a controlling financial interest is determined to be the primary beneficiary of the VIE and is required to consolidate the entity in its financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In addition, a reporting entity is required to reevaluate whether an entity is a VIE, and if the entity is determined to be a VIE, whether the reporting entity is the primary beneficiary of the VIE, periodically upon the occurrence of certain events known as </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">reconsideration events.&nbsp;&nbsp;A loan modified in a troubled debt restructuring (&#x201C;TDR&#x201D;) triggers a reconsideration event.&nbsp;&nbsp;See</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 10, Investments and Variable Interest Entities</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">for additional information.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">(q)&nbsp;&nbsp;Servicing Assets</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">During the fiscal year ended June 30, 2013, the Bank sold $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">17,664,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Small Business Administration (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SBA</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x201C;) </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">loans resulting in a</font><font style="display: inline;"> gain of </font><font style="display: inline;">$2,253,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the sale, the Bank recorded a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">servicing asset of $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">418,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank accounts for its servicing rights in accordance with ASC 860-50</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Servicing Assets and Liabilities</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">,&#x201D; at amortized cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The codification requires that servicing rights acquired through the origination of loans, which are sold with servicing rights retained, are recognized as separate assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Servicing assets are recorded as the difference between the contractual servicing fees and adequate compensation for performing the servicing, and are periodically reviewed and adjusted for any impairment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of impairment recognized, if any, is the amount by which the servicing assets exceed their fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value of the servicing assets is estimated using discounted cash flows based on current market interest rates.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">See </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 1(x) and Note 26, Fair Value of Financial Instruments.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;Servicing rights are amortized in proportion to, and over the period of the related net servicing income.</font>
		</p>

These drafts are presented for payment through an unaffiliated bank and are sent to SWS daily for review and acceptance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon acceptance, the drafts are paid and charged against cash.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">(s) Federal Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS and its subsidiaries file a consolidated federal income tax return.&nbsp;&nbsp;Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the estimated future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the date of the tax rate changes. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Company records net deferred tax assets to the extent the Company believes these assets are more likely than not to be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;In making such determination, the Company considers all available positive and negative evidence, including future reversals of existing taxable temporary differences, projected future taxable income, tax planning strategies and recent financial operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;A valuation allowance is established against deferred tax assets when the Company determines that they are more likely to not be realized than realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event the Company subsequently determines that it would be able to realize deferred income tax assets in excess of their net recorded amount, the Company would reduce the valuation allowance, which would reduce the provision for income taxes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Deferred tax assets derived from operating losses are realized when the Company generates consolidated taxable income within the applicable carry-back and carryforward periods.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Based on an evaluation of the positive and negative evidence, management determined that it was appropriate to increase the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">valuation allowance for </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> remaining deferred tax assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> with the exception of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Bank&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">available for sale securities.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Management determined that an increase in the valuation allowance was appropriate in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2013 after reviewing the impact of our fourth quarter operating results and our fiscal 2014 financial&nbsp;&nbsp;forecast.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Accordingly, the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">C</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">ompany increased its allowance </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$29,998,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$872,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 29, 2012 to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$30,870,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 30, 2013.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">See </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 17, Income Taxes</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> for a detail of the Company&#x2019;s deferred tax assets.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Net holding gains and losses represent the unrealized holding gains and losses on securities available for sale. See </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">9</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">, Securities Available for Sale.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">For the interest rate swaps that are designated and qualify as part of a cash flow hedging relationship, changes in the fair value are recognized in accumulated other comprehensive income to the extent the derivative is effective at offsetting the changes in cash flows being hedged until the hedged item affects earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effective portion of the gain or loss on the derivative is reported as a component of other comprehensive income and reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods during which the hedged transaction affects earnings. Gains and losses on the derivative representing hedge ineffectiveness and changes in fair value of the derivative instruments not designated in a cash flow hedging relationship are recognized in other revenue on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Loss.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">(x) Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Fair value accounting establishes a framework for measuring fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under fair value accounting, fair value refers to the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date in the principal market in which the reporting entity transacts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, fair value should be based on the assumptions market participants would use when pricing the asset or liability.&nbsp;&nbsp;In support of this principle, fair value accounting establishes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the information used to develop those assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value hierarchy gives the highest priority to quoted prices in active markets and the lowest priority to unobservable data.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the standard, fair value measurements are separately disclosed by level within the fair value hierarchy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The standard describes three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair value:&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

						<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Level&nbsp;1</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;&#x2014; Quoted prices in an active market for identical assets or liabilities. The Company values the following assets and liabilities utilizing Level&nbsp;1 inputs:&nbsp;&nbsp;(1)&nbsp;&nbsp;the Company's investment in government guaranteed bonds purchased under the Temporary Liquidity Guarantee Program (&#x201C;TLGP&#x201D;); (2) certain inventories held in the Company's securities owned and securities sold, not yet purchased portfolio; (3) the Company&#x2019;s investment in U.S. Home Systems, Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> (&#x201C;USHS&#x201D;) common stock and (4)</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> the Company&#x2019;s deferred compensation plan&#x2019;s investment in Westwood Holdings Group, Inc.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> (&#x201C;Westwood&#x201D;) common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;Valuation of these instruments does not require a high degree of judgment as the valuations are based on quoted prices in active markets that are readily available.</font></p>
				</td>
			</tr>
		</table></div>

						<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Level&nbsp;2&nbsp;&#x2014; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Observable inputs other than Level 1 prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities. The Company values the following assets and liabilities utilizing Level&nbsp;2 inputs:&nbsp;&nbsp;(1) the Bank&#x2019;s loans measured at fair value</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;(</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">) the Bank&#x2019;s investment in interest rate swaps; (</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">) certain inventories held in the Company&#x2019;s securities owned and securities sold, not yet purchased portfolio; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">) securities in the available for sale portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;These financial instruments are valued by quoted prices that are less frequent than those in active markets or by models that use various assumptions that are derived from or supported by data that is generally observable in the marketplace. Valuations in this category are inherently less reliable than quoted market prices due to the degree of subjectivity involved in determining appropriate methodologies and the applicable underlying observable market assumptions.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font></p>

The Company values the following assets and liabilities utilizing Level 3 inputs:&nbsp;&nbsp;(1) certain inventories held in the Company's securities owned portfolio and (2) the warrants. These financial instruments have significant inputs that cannot be validated by readily determinable market data and generally involve considerable judgment by management.</font></p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The following is a description of the valuation methodologies used for instruments measured at fair value on recurring and non-recurring bases and recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition, as well as the general classification of such instruments pursuant to the valuation hierarchy.</font>
