</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 9.35pt;text-indent: -9.35pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Recurring Fair Value Measurements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Assets Segregated for Regulatory Purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Because quoted market prices are available in an active market, these securities are classified within Level 1 of the valuation hierarchy.&nbsp;&nbsp;These securities consist of government bonds purchased under the TLGP. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Loans measured at fair value.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The fair value of loans for which the fair value option has been elected is calculated based on the present value of expected future discounted cash flows using market interest rates currently being offered for loans with similar terms to borrowers with comparable credit risk.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">These loans are classified within Level 2 of the valuation hierarchy.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Securities Owned and Securities Sold, Not Yet Purchased Portfolio.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Securities classified as Level 1 securities primarily consist of financial instruments whose value is based on quoted market prices such as corporate equity securities and U.S. government and government agency obligations, primarily U.S. treasury securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Securities classified as Level 2 securities include financial instruments that are valued using models or other valuation methodologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;These models are primarily industry standard models that consider various assumptions, including time value, yield curve, volatility factors, current market and contractual prices for the underlying financial instruments, as well as other relevant economic measures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Substantially all of these assumptions are observable in the marketplace, can be derived from observable data or are supported by observable levels at which transactions are executed in the marketplace.&nbsp;&nbsp;Securities in this category include corporate obligations, U.S. government and government agency obligations and municipal obligations.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Securities classified as Level 3 securities are securities whose fair value is estimated based on internally developed models or methodologies, including discounted cash flow, utilizing significant inputs that are generally less readily observable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The models and methodologies consider the quality of the underlying loans, any related secondary market activity and expectations regarding future interest rate movements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in this category are certain corporate equity securities, corporate bonds and municipal auction rate securities.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">At June 29, 2012, the Company held </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">one</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> municipal auction rate bond with a par amount of $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">21,950,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> that was classified as a Level 3 security.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of a trade in a similar security at a value less than par and related market conditions in the first quarter of fiscal 2013, the Company determined that this security should be written down to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">92.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">% of par.&nbsp;&nbsp;The result was a $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">702,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> write down in the first quarter of fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2013, we sold this security with no gain or loss recognized on the transaction.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Securities Available for Sale.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Because quoted market prices are available in an active market, the Company&#x2019;s investment in USHS</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> common stock and the Company&#x2019;s deferred compensation plan&#x2019;s investment in Westwood</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> common stock are classified within Level 1 of the valuation hierarchy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s investments in U.S. government and government agency and municipal obligations held by the Bank as available for sale are valued in a similar manner to the Company&#x2019;s Level 2 securities owned and securities sold, not yet purchased portfolio, noted below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Interest Rate Swaps.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The fair value of interest rate swaps</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">is determined using an income approach incorporating various assumptions, including the term of the swap, the notional amount of the swap, discount rates interpolated based on relevant swap curves, the rate on the fixed leg of the swap and a credit value adjustment for counterparty non-performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The approach also takes into consideration the potential impact of collateralization and netting agreements.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Because s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">ubstantially all of these assumptions are observable in the marketplace, can be derived from observable data or are supported by observable levels at which transactions are executed in the marketplace</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, the intrest rate swaps are classified within Level 2 of the valuation hierarchy</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Warrants.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;The warrants held by Hilltop and Oak Hill are valued using a binomial model which forecasts the Company&#x2019;s potential stock price at certain points in time between the valuation date and expiration date of the warrants.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the Company&#x2019;s stock price, variables in the model include the risk free rate of return, dividend yield, time to maturity and volatility of the Company&#x2019;s stock price.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;The warrants are classified within Level 3 of the valuation hierarchy.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Substantially all of SWS&#x2019;s brokerage assets and liabilities are carried at market value or at amounts which, because of their short-term nature, approximate current fair value.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Non-recurring Fair Value Measurements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 30pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Impaired loans held for investment.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Certain impaired loans are reported at fair value through the recognition of a specific valuation allowance or a partial principal charge-off.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of an impaired loan is primarily determined based on the present value of the loan&#x2019;s expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#x2019;s original effective rate or the </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">15</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 8pt">

			<a href="#IndexToAnnualReport"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:8pt;">Table Of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 30pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">fair value of collateral if the loan is collateral-dependent.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the fair value of collateral is used to measure impairment of a collateral-dependent loan and repayment is dependent on the sale of the collateral, the fair value is adjusted to incorporate estimated costs to sell the collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;Impaired loans that are collateral-dependent are primarily measured for impairment using the fair value of the collateral as determined by third party appraisals using the income approach, recent comparable sales data or a combination thereof.&nbsp;&nbsp;In certain instances it is necessary for management to adjust the appraised value, less estimated costs to sell the collateral, to reflect changes in fair value occurring subsequent to the appraisal date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, impaired loans reported at fair value in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition are classified as Level 3 in the fair value hierarchy.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">REO and other repossessed assets.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">See </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 1(n), </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Real Estate Owned (&#x201C;REO&#x201D;) and Other Repossessed Assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> for discussion of the valuation of these assets. REO and other repossessed assets are valued using Level 3 valuation methodologies as the inputs utilized to determine fair value require significant judgment and estimation.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Other Fair Value Disclosures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The following is a description of the valuation methodologies used for financial instruments not measured at fair value in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition, but for which fair value is required to be disclosed in accordance with ASC 820</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosure</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;See </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 26, Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> for additional information, including the hierarchy levels for these financial instruments.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Securities held to maturity.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Fair values of securities held to maturity are based on the Company&#x2019;s fair value policies regarding U.S. government and government agency obligations discussed above under </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&#x2013; Recurring Fair Value Measurements &#x2013; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Securities Owned and Securities Sold, Not Yet Purchased portfolio</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Loans.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Fair values of loans receivable, including purchased mortgage loans held for investment, are estimated for portfolios of loans with similar characteristics.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loans are segregated by type, such as real estate, commercial and consumer, which are further segregated into fixed and adjustable rate interest terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of loans receivable is calculated by discounting expected future cash flows through the estimated maturity using interest rates currently being offered for loans with similar terms to borrowers of similar credit quality.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Loan fair value estimates include judgments regarding future expected loss experience and risk characteristics.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt -4.5pt 0pt 28.8pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt -4.5pt 0pt 28.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Servicing assets.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">See</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 1(q), </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Servicing Assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> for discussion of the valuation of these assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt -4.5pt 0pt 28.8pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt -4.5pt 0pt 28.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Deposits.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">T</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">he fair value of deposits with no stated maturity, such as interest-bearing checking accounts, passbook savings accounts and advance payments from borrowers for taxes and insurance, is based on current market rates for deposits payable on demand.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of certificates of deposit is based on the discounted value of contractual cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount rate is estimated using the rates currently offered for deposits of similar remaining maturities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 31.5pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Advances from FHLB.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The fair value of advances from FHLB is based on the discounted value of contractual cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount rate is estimated using the rates currently offered for borrowings of similar remaining maturities.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Long-term debt.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The fair value of long-term debt is estimated using a discounted cash flow model with assumptions regarding the factors a market participant would consider in valuing the liability, including credit and liquidity risk.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.8pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">(y) Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The FASB and the SEC have recently issued the following statements and interpretations, which are applicable to SWS.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any other new accounting pronouncements not specifically identified in our disclosures are not applicable to SWS.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">ASU 2011-11, &#x201C;Disclosures about Offsetting Assets and Liabilities&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;"> (&#x201C;ASU 2011-11&#x201D;) as updated by ASU 2013-01, &#x201C;Clarifying the Scope of Disclosures about Offsetting Assets and Liabilities.&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In December 2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-11 which requires entities to disclose both gross and net information about instruments and transactions eligible for offset in the statement of financial position and instruments and transactions subject to an agreement similar to a master netting agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purpose of ASU 2011-11 is to facilitate comparison between entities that prepare their financial statements on a GAAP basis and entities that prepare their financial statements on the basis of International Financial Reporting Standards (&#x201C;IFRS&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2011-11 applies to derivatives, sale and repurchase agreements and reverse sale and repurchase agreements and securities borrowing and lending arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2011-11 is effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2013, and interim periods within those annual periods, the Company&#x2019;s first quarter of fiscal 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect ASU 2011-11 to have a material impact on its financial statements and processes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">2.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:28pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">ASSETS SEGREGATED FOR REGULATORY PURPOSES</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Securities failed to deliver and receive represent the contractual value of securities that have not been delivered or received subsequent to settlement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Securities borrowed and loaned represent deposits made to or received from other broker/dealers relating to these transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;These deposits approximate the market valu</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">e of the underlying securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS clears securities transactions for correspondent broker/dealers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Proprietary settled securities and related transactions for these correspondents are included in the receivable from and payable to brokers, dealers and clearing organizations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS participates in the securities borrowing and lending business by borrowing and lending securities other than those of its clients.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS obtains or releases collateral as prices of the underlying securities fluctuate.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013, SWS had collateral of $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,546,376,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> under securities lending agreements, of which SWS had repledged $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,452,911,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 29, 2012, SWS had collateral of $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,320,024,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> under securities lending agreements, of which SWS had repledged $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,250,328,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">4.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:28pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">RECEIVABLE FROM AND PAYABLE TO CLIENTS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Receivable from and payable to clients include amounts due on cash and margin transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in these amounts are receivable from and payable to noncustomers (as defined by Rule 15c3-3 of the Exchange Act, principally officers, directors and related accounts), which aggregated approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">766,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">10,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, at June 30, 2013 and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">359,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,371,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, at June 29, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Securities owned by customers and noncustomers that collateralize the receivable are not reflected in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS pays interest on certain customer "free credit" balances available for reinvestment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The aggregate balance of such funds was approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">304,016,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">308,669,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and during fiscal year 2013, the weighted average interest rate and the interest rate paid on these balances was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">0.02</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">%.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2012, the interest rates paid on these balances ranged from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">0.02</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">% to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">0.05</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">%, with a weighted average interest rate paid of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">0.04</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">%.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS maintains an allowance for doubtful accounts which represents amounts, that in the judgment of management, are necessary to adequately absorb losses from known and inherent risks in receivables from customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Provisions made to this allowance are charged to operations and are included in other expense in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Loss.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012, all unsecured customer receivables are provided for in this allowance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The allowance was $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">168,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">117,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012, respectively.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Loans are classified as non-performing when they are 90 days or more past due as to principal or interest or when reasonable doubt exists as to timely collectibility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank uses a standardized review process to determine which loans should be placed on non-accrual status.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the time a loan is placed on non-accrual status, previously accrued and uncollected interest is reversed against interest income.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest income on non-accrual loans is subsequently recognized to the extent cash payments are received for loans where full collection is likely.&nbsp;&nbsp;For loans where full collection is not likely, interest payments are applied to the outstanding principal and income is only recognized if full payment is made.&nbsp;&nbsp;The average recorded investment in non-accrual loans at June 30, 2013 and June 30, 2012 was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$25,516,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;a</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">nd </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$51,663,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;For fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011, interest income recorded on non-accrual loans prior to being placed on non-accrual status totaled approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$266,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$1,186,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$1,218,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In certain circumstances, the Bank modifies the terms of its loans to a troubled borrower.&nbsp;&nbsp;Modifications may include extending the maturity date, reducing the stated interest rate, rescheduling future cash flows or some combination thereof.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank accounts for the modification as a TDR.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Loans that have been modified in a TDR continue to be considered restructured until paid in full.&nbsp;&nbsp;These loans, including loans restructured in the prior 12 months that defaulted during the period, are individually evaluated for impairment taking into consideration payment status, collateral value, and the probability of collecting scheduled principal and interest payments when due.&nbsp;&nbsp;A specific allowance for an impaired loan that has been modified in a TDR is established when the loan&#x2019;s fair value is lower than its recorded investment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the historical loss rates of loans modified in TDR&#x2019;s, by portfolio segment, are factored into the formula utilized to determine the general allowance for probable loan losses.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 9.35pt;text-indent: -9.35pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		</p>

Interest on these amounts is accrued and is included in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition in other liabilities.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Securities sold under repurchase agreements at June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012 were $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">37,012,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">27,465,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">9.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">SECURITIES AVAILABLE FOR SALE</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS Group owns shares of common stock of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Westwood</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, which it classifies as securities available for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the shares of common stock owned by SWS Group, the Bank owns U.S. government and government agency and municipal obligations that are available for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;The unrealized holding gains (losses), net of tax, related to these securities are recorded as a separate component of stockholders&#x2019; equity on the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> At June 29, 2012, SWS Group also owned shares of common stock of U.S. Home Systems, Inc. (&#x201C;USHS&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;On October 26, 2012, a special meeting of the stockholders of USHS was held requesting an affirmative vote of the stockholders to adopt a proposed acquisition agreement, among other proposals.&nbsp;&nbsp;USHS announced on October 29, 2012 that the acquisition agreement between USHS and The Home Depot, Inc. was approved and that, as a result, all outstanding shares of its common stock, including the shares of USHS common stock held by SWS, would be purchased for a price of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$12.50</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS Group&#x2019;s shares of USHS common stock were purchased in November 2012 and as a result, the Company recognized a realized gain of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$3,550,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in net gains on principal transactions and a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$2,308,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> ( </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$3,550,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">,net of tax) reclassification adjustment from accumulated other comprehensive income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 9.35pt;text-indent: -9.35pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

amount to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">5,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loan was renewed on September 26, 2012 with a maturity date of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">January 2, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2012, the loan was paid in full.&nbsp;&nbsp;On December 31, 2012, the Bank executed a new loan agreement with one of the partnerships for $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">5,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> with a maturity date of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013, the outstanding balance was $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">2,549,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loan bears interest at a rate of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">4.25</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">% per annum and interest is due monthly. The Bank earned approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">166,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">243,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">250,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in interest income in fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively, on these loans. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:0pt;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In April 2012, the Bank acquired an interest in a private investment fund to obtain additional credit for its obligations under the CRA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank has committed to invest $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">3,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in the fund and to date has invested </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$180,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in the fund and recorded net losses of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$118,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> during fiscal 2013. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Company&#x2019;s investments in and the Bank&#x2019;s loan to these funds may be limited by a portion of the Dodd-Frank Act called the Volcker Rule, which has proposed implementing regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management will monitor the final rules implementing the Volcker Rule once they are published to determine what impact, if any, the final rules would have on the Company&#x2019;s investments and loan to these funds.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Variable Interest Entities.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">VIE&#x2019;s include partnerships, limited liability companies, trusts, or other legal entities that do not have sufficient equity to finance their activities without additional subordinated financial support from other parties, or whose investors lack one of three characteristics associated with owning a controlling financial interest. Those characteristics are: (1)&nbsp;the direct or indirect ability to make decisions about an entity&#x2019;s activities through voting rights or similar rights; (2)&nbsp;the obligation to absorb the expected losses of an entity, if they occur and (3)&nbsp;the right to receive the expected residual returns of the entity, if they occur. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">GAAP requires VIEs to be consolidated by the party that has both (1)&nbsp;the ability to direct the VIE&#x2019;s activities that most significantly impact the entity&#x2019;s economic performance and (2)&nbsp;who is exposed to a majority of the VIE&#x2019;s expected losses and/or residual returns (i.e., meets the definition of the primary beneficiary). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The loans to commercial borrowers noted in the table below meet the definition of a VIE because the legal entities have a total equity investment at risk that is not sufficient to permit the entity to finance its activities without additional subordinated financial support; however, the Company is not the primary beneficiary of the legal entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has customary lender&#x2019;s rights and remedies, as provided in the related promissory notes and loan agreements, but does not have the power to direct the activities of the legal entities that most significantly impact the borrowers&#x2019; economic performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Company has not provided the borrowers with any form of support outside of the contractual loan obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, the entities are not consolidated in the Company&#x2019;s financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The carrying amount of the Company&#x2019;s recorded investment in these loans is included in loans, net of allowance for loan losses in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;See additional discussion in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 5, Loans and Allowance for Probable Loan Losses</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> for information related to the loans modified in TDR&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">11.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">INTEREST RATE SWAPS</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In fiscal 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">the Bank entered into forward-start interest rate swaps to mitigate risk from its </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">exposure to variability in interest payments on the Bank&#x2019;s variable rate deposits</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;The Bank&#x2019;s forward-start interest rate swaps</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">exchange fixed for variable interest payments beginning at a pre-specified date in the future according to the terms </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">the swap agreements</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and are designated as cash flow hedges</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">As of June 30, 2013, the notional amount of interest rate swap agreements </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">designated as cash flow hedging instruments </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$100,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">with a fair value of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$1,789,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> included in other assets on the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In addition, interest rate swaps</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">are used by the Bank to manage interest rate risk on certain fixed rate loans funded with variable rate deposits which exposes the Bank to potential variability in its net interest margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;These fixed rate loans include terms matching the interest rate swaps</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">and are recorded at fair value under the fair value option election. As of June 30, 2013, the notional amount of interest rate swaps</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">outstanding related to fixed rate loan transactions was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$13,902,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> with a fair value of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$145,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> included in other assets on the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">For fiscal year 2013, gains recognized in other revenue </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Loss </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">as a result of changes in fair value of the interest rate swaps were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$145,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">12.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">INTANGIBLE ASSETS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">On </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">March 22, 2006</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, the Company entered into an agreement with TD Ameritrade Holding Corporation, ("Ameritrade") to transfer Ameritrade&#x2019;s correspondent clearing clients to the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;This transaction closed in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">July 2006</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of this transaction, the Company recorded a customer relationship intangible of $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">5,060,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The intangible asset was amortized over a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">five</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> year period at a rate based on the estimated future economic benefit of the customer relationships.&nbsp;&nbsp;This intangible asset was fully amortized in July 2011 and SWS recognized approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">6,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">785,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of amortization expense in fiscal years 2012 and 2011, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">13.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">SHORT-TERM BORROWINGS</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Brokerage.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;text-decoration:underline;">Uncommitted lines of credit</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Southwest Securities has credit arrangements with commercial banks, which include broker loan lines up to $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">375,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;These lines of credit are used primarily to finance securities owned, securities held for correspondent broker/dealer accounts, receivables in customers&#x2019; margin accounts and underwriting activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;These lines may also be used to release pledged collateral against day loans. These credit arrangements are provided on an &#x201C;as offered&#x201D; basis and are not committed lines of credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;These arrangements can be terminated at any time by the lender. Any outstanding balance under these credit arrangements is due on demand and bears interest at rates indexed to the federal funds rate (</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">0.07</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">% at June 30, 2013 and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">0.09</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">% at June 29, 2012). The total amount of borrowings available under these lines of credit is reduced by the amount available under the options trading unsecured letter of credit, referenced below.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013, the amount outstanding under these secured arrangements was $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">86,500,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, which was collateralized by securities held for firm accounts valued at $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">120,568,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 29, 2012, the amount outstanding under these secured arrangements was $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">22,500,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, which was collateralized by securities held for firm accounts valued at $</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">80,125,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<a name="lastkeyword"></a><a name="keyword"></a><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Periodic reviews of the carrying amount of deferred tax assets are made to determine if the establishment of a valuation allowance is necessary when it is more likely than not that all or a portion of a deferred tax asset will not be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;In assessing the realization of deferred tax assets, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">management</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> considers all available evidence, both positive and negative from the following expected sources of income:&nbsp;&nbsp;expected </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">future </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">reversal</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of deferred tax assets and liabilities, projected future taxable income, cumulative losses in recent years and tax planning strategies. In making such judgments, significant weight is given to evidence that can</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> be objectively verified.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASC </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">740, &#x201C;Income Taxes&#x201D; provides that a cumulative loss in recent years is significant negative evidence in considering whether deferred tax assets are realizable and also restricts the reliance on projections of future taxable income to support the recovery of deferred tax assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the Company&#x2019;s current financial forecasts indicate that sufficient taxable income </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">should</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> be generated in the future to ultimately realize the existing deferred tax benefits</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">these forecasts are subject to a number of assumptions and there can be no assurance that these forecasts will be achieved.&nbsp;&nbsp;T</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">h</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">e</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">se forecasts were not considered to constitute sufficient positive evidence</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, as required by GAAP, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">to overcome the observable negative evidence associated with the cumulative loss positions. The Company previously had an allowance for deferred tax assets associated with its capital losses from investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on an evaluation of the positive and negative evidence, management determined that it was appropriate to increase the valuation allowance for its remaining deferred tax assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> except</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> for </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">the Bank&#x2019;s securities available for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">C</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">ompany increased its allowance </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$29,998,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> from </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$872,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 29, 2012 to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$30,870,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 30, 2013. </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Banking</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> The Bank is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by federal agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quantitative measures, established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy, require maintaining minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the table below) of total and Tier I capital (as defined in 12 CFR 165 and 12 CFR 167) to risk-weighted assets (as defined) and of Tier I (core) capital (as defined) to adjusted assets (as defined).&nbsp;&nbsp;Federal statutes and OCC regulations have established five capital categories for federal savings banks: well-capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized, and critically undercapitalized. The federal banking agencies have jointly specified by regulation the relevant capital level for each category. An institution is defined as well-capitalized when its total risk-based capital ratio is at least 10.00%, its Tier I risk-based capital ratio is at least 6.00%, its Tier I (core) capital ratio is at least 5.00%, and it is not subject to any federal supervisory order or directive to meet a specific capital level.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">At June 30, 2013, the Bank was deemed to be well capitalized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Until terminated on January 14, 2013, the Bank was restricted by and subject to the Order to Cease and Desist, Order No. WN-11-003, effective on February 4, 2011 (the &#x201C;Order&#x201D;), originally issued by</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">the Office of Thrift Supervision and then administered by the OCC.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the termination of the Order on January 14, 2013, the Bank committed to the OCC that the Bank would, among other things:&nbsp;&nbsp;(i) adhere to the Bank&#x2019;s written business and capital plan as amended from time to time and (ii) maintain a Tier I (core) capital ratio at least equal to nine percent (9%) and a total risk-based capital ratio of at least twelve percent (12%).</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Profit Sharing/401(k) Plan.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS has a defined contribution profit sharing/401(k) plan covering substantially all of its employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;Employer provided profit sharing plan benefits become fully vested after </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">six</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> years of service by the participant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Profit sharing contributions are accrued and funded at SWS&#x2019;s discretion.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">no</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> profit sharing contributions in fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company contributes a matching contribution equal to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">100%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of the participant&#x2019;s salary reduction amount not in excess of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">4%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of the individual&#x2019;s compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS&#x2019;s matching contributions vest immediately and the expense totaled approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$4,086,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$3,979,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$4,133,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Employees have an option to purchase shares of SWS Group&#x2019;s common stock held as an investment in the 401(k) plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 401(k) may purchase up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,500,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of SWS Group&#x2019;s common stock and at June 30, 2013, the total number of shares available for future purchases was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,003,764</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Deferred Compensation Plan.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS Group provides a deferred compensation plan for eligible officers and employees to defer a portion of their bonus compensation and commissions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The assets of the deferred compensation plan include investments in SWS Group common stock, Westwood common stock and COLI.&nbsp;&nbsp;Investments in SWS Group common stock are carried at cost and are held as treasury stock with an offsetting deferred compensation liability in the equity section of the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Investments in Westwood common stock are carried at market value and recorded as securities available for sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;Investments in COLI are carried at the cash surrender value of the insurance policies and recorded in other assets in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.&nbsp; </font>
