		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Restricted Stock Plan.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The 2003 Restricted Stock Plan allows for awards of up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,250,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> shares of SWS Group&#x2019;s common stock to SWS&#x2019;s directors, officers and employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;No more than </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">300,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of the authorized shares may be newly issued shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2003 Restricted Stock Plan terminates on </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">August 21, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;On November 15, 2012, the stockholders of SWS Group, Inc. approved the adoption of the 2012 Restricted Stock Plan. The 2012 Restricted Stock Plan allows for awards of stock to SWS&#x2019;s directors, officers and employees and authorizes up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">2,630,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> shares of SWS&#x2019;s common stock to be delivered pursuant to awards granted under the 2012 Restricted Stock Plan. The 2012 Restricted Stock Plan terminates on </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">November 15, 2022</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">. The vesting period for awards is determined on an individual basis by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In general, restricted stock granted to employees under the 2012 and 2003 Restricted Stock Plans vests pro-rata over a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">three</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> year period or is subject to a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">four</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> year cliff vesting schedule, and restricted stock granted to non-employee directors vests on the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">one</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> year anniversary of the date of grant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;background-color:;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">During fiscal 2011, the Board of Directors approved grants to various officers and employees totaling </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">64,151</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> shares with a weighted average market share.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2012, the Board of Directors approved grants to various officers and employees totaling </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">348,810</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> shares with a weighted average market value of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$7.02</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;During fiscal 2013, the Board of Directors approved grants to various officers and employees totaling </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">65,079</font><font style="display: Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$4.84</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of these grants, SWS recorded deferred compensation in additional paid in capital of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$3,160,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;For fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011, SWS recognized compensation expense of approximately </font><font style="display: 		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">On March 17, 2011 in conjunction with the transaction with Hilltop and Oak Hill, the Board of Directors created the Series A Preferred Stock, par value </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$1.00</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">17,400</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> authorized shares of Series A Preferred Stock, and no shares are </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">issued</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> or </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">outstanding</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;If any shares of Series A Preferred Stock are issued, the Series A Preferred Stock will not be entitled to vote with the common stock and will be convertible into shares of common stock at a fixed conversion ratio of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">1,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> shares of common stock for each share of Series A Preferred Stock outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;The conversion ratio is subject to certain anti-dilution adjustments for extraordinary corporate transactions, such as stock splits, dividends and combinations, the issuance of stock purchase rights, debt or asset distributions (including cash), tender offers or exchange offers and entry into a shareholder rights plan. Each share of Series A Preferred Stock would automatically convert into shares of common stock if such shares were transferred by Hilltop or Oak Hill to a non-affiliate. See additional discussion concerning the Series A Preferred Stock in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Note 16, Debt Issued with Stock Purchase Warrants.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Commitments and Contingencies</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;">.&nbsp; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Litigation.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In the general course of its brokerage business and the business of clearing for other brokerage firms, SWS Group and/or its subsidiaries have been named as defendants in various lawsuits and arbitration proceedings.&nbsp;&nbsp;These claims allege, among other things, violations of various federal and state securities laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank is also involved in certain legal claims and actions arising in the ordinary course of business.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management believes that resolution of these claims will not result in any material adverse effect on SWS&#x2019;s consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Company has been named as a defendant in three lawsuits related to a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$35,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> bond offering that was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">40%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> underwritten by M.L. Stern &amp; Co., LLC.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS Group purchased M.L. Stern &amp; Co., LLC in 2008.&nbsp;&nbsp;The offering took place in November 2005, and the lawsuit was filed in November 2009.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The lawsuits are in the discovery stage and the ultimate amount of liability associated with them cannot currently be determined.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the Company believes it is at least reasonably possible that a loss related to this matter will be incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012, the Company had a recorded liability of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$1,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> related to this matter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Contingency.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">In February 2011, a limited partnership venture capital fund in which the Company invested received a proposed assessment of transferee liability from the IRS for the tax period ended December 31, 2005.&nbsp;&nbsp;The proposed assessment is approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$8,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;">, not including penalties of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$3,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company would be responsible for approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,870,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the proposed assessment including penalties based on its partnership interest.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest is also accruing on this proposed assessment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The matter relates to certain transactions that occurred during 2005 concerning one of the limited partnership venture capital fund&#x2019;s subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The limited partnership venture capital fund engaged tax counsel and filed a Letter of Protest with the IRS in April 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management of the limited partnership venture capital fund believes that the ultimate outcome will be favorable; however, the limited partnership venture capital fund can give no assurance that it will prevail.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Leases.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp;SWS leases its offices and certain data processing equipment used in its brokerage operations under non-cancelable operating lease agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognizes escalating lease payments on a straight line basis over the term of each respective lease with the difference between cash payment and rent expense recorded as deferred rent and included in other liabilities in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Rental expense for facilities and equipment leases for fiscal years 2013, 2012 and 2011 aggregated approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$10,349,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$10,944,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$11,604,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Venture Capital Fund. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> The Bank has committed to invest </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$3,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$2,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in two limited partnership equity funds.&nbsp;&nbsp;These commitments end in fiscal 2017 and fiscal 2020, respectively, unless the limited partners elect to terminate the commitment period at an earlier date in accordance with the terms of the partnership agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also,&nbsp;&nbsp;in April 2012, the Bank acquired an interest in a private investment fund to obtain additional credit for its obligations under the CRA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank has committed to invest </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$3,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in the fund.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of June 30, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$180,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in contributions have been made by the Bank to this fund.&nbsp;&nbsp;These investments are subject to the Volcker Rule provisions of the Dodd-Frank Act, which limits the Bank to a </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">3%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> ownership interest in any private equity.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The rule </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">is expected to</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> become effective on or about </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">June 21, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Thereafter, financial institutions can request up to three additional one year extensions from the FRB, and the FRB can grant up to a five year extension for investments in illiquid funds made on or before </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">May 21, 2010</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, funds that are &#x201C;designed primarily to promote the public welfare&#x201D; are not subject to the rule as proposed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank&#x2019;s ownership percentage in one of the limited partnership equity funds and the private investment fund are greater than 3% and would qualify as illiquid funds.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, these investments may qualify as &#x201C;designed primarily to promote the public welfare&#x201D; as the Bank invests in these funds</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> as a cost effective way of meeting its obligations under the CRA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank&#x2019;s ownership percentage in the other limited partnership equity fund is less than 3%.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Management will monitor the terms of the final rule implementing the Volcker Rule when it is published, however, until that time it is uncertain how the terms of the final rule will impact the Bank&#x2019;s investments.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Underwriting.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Through its participation in underwriting corporate and municipal securities, SWS could expose itself to material risk that securities SWS has committed to purchase cannot be sold at the initial offering price.&nbsp;&nbsp;Federal and state securities laws and regulations also affect the activities of underwriters and impose substantial potential liabilities for violations in connection with sales of securities by underwriters to the public.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013, the Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">$150,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in total potential liabilities due under outstanding underwriting arrangements. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Guarantees. </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Bank faces the risk of credit loss under commitments to extend credit and stand-by letters of credit up to the contractual amount of these instruments in the event of breach by the other party to the instrument.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for instruments reported on the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.</font>
		</p>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In the ordinary course of business, the Bank enters into loan agreements where the Bank commits to lend a specified amount of money to a borrower. At any point in time, there could be amounts that have not been advanced on the loan to the borrower, representing unfunded commitments, as well as amounts that have been disbursed but repaid, which are available for re-borrowing under a revolving line of credit. As of June 30, 2013, the Bank had commitments of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$28,153,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> relating to revolving lines of credit and unfunded commitments. In addition, as of June 30, 2013, the Bank had approved unfunded new loans in the amount of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$36,570,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Century Schoolbook;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is no violation of any condition established in the contract.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require the payment of a fee.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since many of the commitments are expected to expire unused, the total Bank&#x2019;s commitments do not necessarily represent future cash requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank evaluates the customer&#x2019;s creditworthiness on a case-by-case basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount and type of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary by the Bank upon extension of credit, varies and is based on management&#x2019;s credit evaluation of the counterparty.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank did not incur any significant losses on its commitments in fiscal 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, management does not believe the Bank will incur material losses as a result of its outstanding commitments at June 30, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company provides representations and warranties to counterparties in connection with a variety of commercial transactions and occasionally indemnifies counterparties against potential losses caused by the breach of those representations and warranties.&nbsp;&nbsp;These indemnification obligations generally are standard contractual indemnities and are entered into in the normal course of business.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum potential amount of future payments that the Company could be required to make under these indemnities cannot be estimated.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the Company believes that it is unlikely it will have to make material payments under these arrangements and has not recorded any contingent liability in the consolidated financial statements for these indemnities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Southwest Securities is a member of multiple exchanges and clearinghouses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the membership agreements, members are generally required to guarantee the performance of other members.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, if a member becomes unable to satisfy its obligations to the clearinghouse, other members would be required to meet shortfalls.&nbsp;&nbsp;To mitigate these performance risks, the exchanges and clearinghouses often require members to post collateral.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS&#x2019;s maximum potential liability under these arrangements cannot be quantified.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the potential for the Company to be required to make payments under these arrangements is unlikely.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, the Company has not recorded any contingent liability in the consolidated financial statements for these arrangements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">25. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">AFFILIATE TRANSACTIONS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Clients and correspondents of SWS have the option to invest in a savings account called Bank Insured Deposits at the Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;These funds are FDIC insured up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$250,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The funds are considered core deposits and are the primary funding source for the Bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Bank&#x2019;s total core deposits were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$993,871,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$1,062,491,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> at June 30, 2013 and 2012, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2013 and June 29, 2012, clients of Southwest Securities had invested </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$878,434,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$930,741,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, in Bank Insured Deposits.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Two</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> directors together with certain members of their families owned approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">64%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century no loan participations outstanding with the local bank.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 30, 2012, the loan participations had </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">outstanding balances of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$1,404,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">, which were collateralized by foreclosed property.&nbsp;&nbsp;During the third quarter of fiscal 2013, the property collateralizing the foreclosed loan was sold for </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$4,339,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> resulting in a gain on sale of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$43,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">holding company</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> received </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$952,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> in proceeds from the substantially the same as those participations sold by the Bank to unrelated banks.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The Company holds </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$3,505,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> of corporate obligation bonds currently valued at </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">$120,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The corporate bonds are valued using a discounted cash flow model with observable market data, however, due to the distressed nature of these bonds, the Company has determined that these bonds should be valued at Level 3.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:115%;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">The </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">w</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">arrants are valued quarterly using a binomial model that considers the following variables: price and volatility of the Company&#x2019;s stock, treasury yield, annual dividend and the remaining life of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">w</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">arrants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The derived volatility estimate considers both the historical and implied forward volatility of the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The primary drivers of the value of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">w</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">arrants are the price and volatility of the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;As the volatility and/or stock price increase, the value of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">w</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">arrants increase as well.&nbsp;&nbsp;The movement of these two variables will amplify or offset one another depending on the direction and velocity of their movements.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">w</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">arrants will lose time value as they near their contractual expiration date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">27. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;width:36pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS WITH OFF-STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL CONDITION RISK</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In the normal course of business, the broker/dealer subsidiaries engage in activities involving the execution, settlement and financing of various securities transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;These activities may expose SWS to off-statement of financial condition credit and market risks in the event the customer or counterparty is unable to fulfill its contractual obligation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such risks may be increased by volatile trading markets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">As part of its normal brokerage activities, SWS sells securities not yet purchased (short sales) for its own account.&nbsp;&nbsp;The establishment of short positions exposes SWS to off-statement of financial condition market risk if prices increase, as SWS may be obligated to acquire the securities at prevailing market prices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS seeks to control the risks associated with its customer activities, including those of customer accounts of its correspondents for which it provides clearing services, by requiring customers to maintain margin collateral in compliance with various regulatory and internal guidelines.&nbsp;&nbsp;The required margin levels are monitored daily and, pursuant to such guidelines, customers are required to deposit additional collateral or to reduce positions when necessary.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">A portion of SWS&#x2019;s customer activity involves short sales and the writing of option contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such transactions may require SWS to purchase or sell financial instruments at prevailing market prices in order to fulfill the customer&#x2019;s obligations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">At times, SWS lends money using reverse repurchase agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;These positions are collateralized by U.S. government and government agency securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such transactions may expose SWS to off-statement of financial condition risk in the event such borrowers do not repay the loans and the value of collateral held is less than that of the underlying receivable.&nbsp;&nbsp;These agreements provide SWS with the right to maintain the relationship between market value of the collateral and the receivable.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">SWS arranges secured financing by pledging securities owned and unpaid customer securities for short-term borrowings to satisfy margin deposits of clearing organizations.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS also actively participates in the borrowing and lending of securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event the counterparty in these and other securities loaned transactions is unable to return such securities pledged or borrowed or to repay the deposit placed with them, SWS may be exposed to the risks of acquiring the securities at prevailing market prices or holding collateral possessing a market value less than that of the related pledged securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;SWS seeks to </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:CG Times (W1);font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F-</font><font style="display: inline;">54</font>

		</p>

			<a href="#IndexToAnnualReport"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:8pt;">Table Of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;">control the risks by monitoring the market value of securities pledged and requiring adjustments of collateral levels where necessary.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Bank is a party to financial instruments with off-statement of financial condition risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;These financial instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk in excess of the amount recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition.</font>

		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<a name="Report_of_Independent_Registered_Public2"></a><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Board of Directors and Shareholders</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">SWS Group, Inc.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of SWS Group, Inc. (a Delaware corporation) and subsidiaries (collectively, the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) as of June 30, 2013, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Internal Control&#x2014;Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). The Company&#x2019;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting appearing under Item 9A of the Company&#x2019;s annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended June 30, 2013. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2013, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;">Internal Control&#x2014;Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;"> issued by COSO.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.2pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Century Schoolbook;font-size:9pt;">financial statements of the Company as of and for the year ended June 30, 2013, and our report dated September 6, 2013 expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements.</font>
		</p>
